Automorphisms of profinite mapping class groups

Marco Boggi Address: UFF - Instituto de Matemática e Estatística - Niterói - RJ 24210-200, Brazil. Email address: marco.boggi@gmail.com
Abstract.

For S=Sg,nS=S_{g,n} a closed orientable differentiable surface of genus gg from which nn points have been removed, such that χ⁡(S)=2−2​g−n<0\chi(S)=2-2g-n<0, let P​Γ​(S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S) be the pure mapping class group of SS and P​Γ^​(S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) and P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) be, respectively, its profinite and its congruence completions, the latter being identified with the image of the natural representation P​Γ^​(S)→Out⁡(π^1​(S)){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)\to\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(S)) (where π^1​(S){\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(S) is the profinite completion of the fundamental group of the surface SS). We determine the automorphism groups of procongruence completions under a natural rigidity condition, and show that the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group embeds into the outer automorphism group of the profinite completion.

Let Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)) and Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) be the groups of outer automorphisms which preserve the conjugacy class of a procyclic subgroup generated by a nonseparating Dehn twist (a condition trivially satisfied for g=0g=0). Our main result gives that, for χ⁡(S)<g−2\chi(S)<g-2 and (g,n)≠(1,2)(g,n)\neq(1,2), there is a natural isomorphism:

Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))≅Σn×GT^,\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\Sigma_{n}\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}},

where Σn\Sigma_{n} is the symmetric group on nn letters and GT^\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} denotes the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group. We also prove that, for χ⁡(S)<g−2\chi(S)<g-2, there is a natural faithful representation GT^↪Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S))\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)).

AMS Subject Classification: Primary 20F34; Secondary 20E18, 20E26, 14G32, 14D23.

1. Introduction

Let S=Sg,nS=S_{g,n} be a closed orientable differentiable surface of genus g⁡(S)=gg(S)=g from which n⁡(S)=nn(S)=n points have been removed. We denote by χ⁡(S)=2−2​g−n\chi(S)=2-2g-n the Euler characteristic of SS, which we assume to be negative, and by d⁡(S)d(S) the modular dimension of SS, that is to say the number of moduli of a Riemann surface diffeomorphic to SS. More precisely, to the topological surface SS, we associate the moduli stacks ℳ⁡(S){\mathcal{M}}(S), which parameterizes smooth projective curves whose complex models are diffeomorphic to SS, and P​ℳ​(S)\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S), which parameterizes the same curves but on which an order of the punctures has been fixed. They are smooth irreducible DM stacks defined over Spec⁡(ℤ)\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{Z}) of dimension d⁡(S)=3​g−3+nd(S)=3g-3+n.

We let Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) be the mapping class group of SS, that is to say the group of isotopy classes of orientation preserving diffeomorphisms of SS, and P​Γ​(S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S) the pure mapping class group of SS, that is to say the kernel of the natural representation Γ⁡(S)→Σn⁡(S){\Gamma}(S)\to\Sigma_{n(S)}, where Σn⁡(S)\Sigma_{n(S)} denotes the symmetric group on the punctures of SS. For an algebraic stack XX over Spec⁡(ℤ)\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{Z}) and a field 𝕂\mathbb{K}, let X𝕂:=X×Spec⁡(𝕂)X_{\mathbb{K}}:=X\times\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{K}). The groups Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) and P​Γ​(S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S) can then be identified, respectively, with the topological fundamental groups of the complex DM stacks ℳ​(S)ℂ{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{C}} and P​ℳ​(S)ℂ\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{C}}.

A classical rigidity result of Ivanov states that, for g≥3g\geq 3, all automorphisms of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) are induced by the inner automorphisms of the extended mapping class group, so that the outer automorphism group of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) is a cyclic group of order 22 (cf. [20]). McCarthy later computed this group also in genus ≤2\leq 2 (cf. [23]). If we let Aut𝕀0⁡(Γ⁡(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\Gamma}(S)) be the group of automorphisms of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) which preserve the conjugacy class of a cyclic subgroup generated by a nonseparating Dehn twist and Out𝕀0⁡(Γ⁡(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\Gamma}(S)) be its quotient by the group of inner automorphisms, all the previous results can be stated in a uniform way by saying that there are, for d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, a natural isomorphism:

Out𝕀0⁡(Γ⁡(S))≅{±1};\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\Gamma}(S))\cong\{\pm 1\};

and, for d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1 and S≠S1,2S\neq S_{1,2}, a natural isomorphism:

Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ​(S))≅Σn⁡(S)×{±1},\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S))\cong\Sigma_{n(S)}\times\{\pm 1\},

where the symmetric group Σn⁡(S)\Sigma_{n(S)} identifies with Inn⁡(Γ⁡(S))/Inn⁡(P​Γ​(S))\operatorname{Inn}({\Gamma}(S))/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S)) and {±1}\{\pm 1\} with its centralizer in Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S)).

Note that, for d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1 and Z⁡(Γ⁡(S))={1}Z({\Gamma}(S))=\{1\}, namely for (g,n)≠(0,4),(1,1),(1,2)(g,n)\neq(0,4),(1,1),(1,2) and (2,0)(2,0), the 𝕀0\mathbb{I}_{0}-condition is always satisfied. However, for Z⁡(Γ⁡(S))≠{1}Z({\Gamma}(S))\neq\{1\}, for instance, we have that Aut𝕀0⁡(Γ⁡(S))⊊Aut⁡(Γ⁡(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\Gamma}(S))\subsetneq\operatorname{Aut}({\Gamma}(S)) (cf. [23, Theorem 1, (3)]).

In this paper, we determine the automorphism groups of the congruence completions of mapping class groups.

The profinite mapping class group Γ^​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) and the pure profinite mapping class group P​Γ^​(S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) are, respectively, the profinite completions of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) and P​Γ​(S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S). The procongruence mapping class group Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) and the pure procongruence mapping class group P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) are, respectively, the images of Γ^​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) and P​Γ^​(S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) in the profinite group Out⁡(π^1​(S))\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(S)).

The congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups asks whether the natural epimorphism Γ^​(S)→Γˇ​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S), or equivalently P​Γ^​(S)→P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S), is an isomorphism. This is known to be true only for g⁡(S)≤2g(S)\leq 2 (cf. [2] and [5], for instance).

Let 𝒞⁡(S)→ℳ⁡(S){\mathscr{C}}(S)\to{\mathcal{M}}(S) and P​𝒞​(S)→P​ℳ​(S)\mathrm{P}{\mathscr{C}}(S)\to\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S) be the universal punctured curves. The profinite mapping class groups Γ^​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) and P​Γ^​(S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) then identify, respectively, with the étale fundamental groups of ℳ​(S)ℚ¯{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} and P​ℳ​(S)ℚ¯\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}, while the procongruence mapping class groups Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) and P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) identify, respectively, with the images of the universal monodromy representations associated to the curves 𝒞​(S)ℚ¯→ℳ​(S)ℚ¯{\mathscr{C}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\to{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} and P​𝒞​(S)ℚ¯→P​ℳ​(S)ℚ¯\mathrm{P}{\mathscr{C}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\to\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}.

By a classical result of Grossman the natural homomorphism Γ​(S)→Γˇ​(S){\Gamma}(S)\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S) is injective and so, in particular, we also have an embedding Γ​(S)↪Γ^​(S){\Gamma}(S)\hookrightarrow{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S). We then identify Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) with its image in Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) (resp. Γ^​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)). Hence, we associate to a simple closed curve γ{\gamma} on SS the Dehn twist τγ∈Γ⁡(S)⊂Γˇ​(S)\tau_{\gamma}\in{\Gamma}(S)\subset{\check{\Gamma}}(S) (resp. ⊂Γ^​(S)\subset{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)). The set of profinite Dehn twists in Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) (resp. Γ^​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)) is the closure of the set of Dehn twists.

A basic advantage of dealing with procongruence mapping class groups is that they have a well developed combinatorial theory (cf. [3], [4] and [5]). In fact, for the procongruence mapping class group Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S), there is a more intrinsic description of profinite Dehn twists in terms of profinite simple closed curves on SS (cf. Section 2.6 and [3, Section 4]).

A fundamental feature of mapping class groups is that, when the center is trivial, automorphisms preserve the conjugacy classes of Dehn twists. In the profinite setting, essentially thanks to a result by Hoshi, Minamide and Mochizuki (cf. [16, Corollary C]), this is known to be true in genus 00 (cf. [8, Theorem 6.6]) but remains a major open problem in positive genus.

It is therefore natural to restrict to automorphisms preserving the conjugacy classes of profinite Dehn twists (the so called inertia condition). A key result of this paper is that it is in fact sufficient to impose the inertia condition only on nonseparating Dehn twists (cf. Theorem 3.12).

Under this natural rigidity condition, we obtain a complete classification of the automorphism groups of congruence completions of mapping class groups in terms of the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group GT^\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} introduced by Drinfeld in [9].

To be more precise, let Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) (resp. Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))) be the group of automorphisms of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) (resp. P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) which preserve the conjugacy class of a procyclic subgroup generated by a nonseparating Dehn twist and let Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)), Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) be the corresponding outer automorphism groups. Our main result provides a complete classification of these automorphism groups (Theorem 6.1 is in fact somewhat more general):

Theorem A.
  1. (i)

    For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, there is a natural isomorphism:

    Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))≅GT^.\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}.
  2. (ii)

    For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1 and S≠S1,2S\neq S_{1,2}, there is a natural isomorphism:

    Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))≅Σn⁡(S)×GT^,\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\Sigma_{n(S)}\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}},

    where the symmetric group Σn⁡(S)\Sigma_{n(S)} identifies with Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))/Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) and GT^\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} with the centralizer of this subgroup.

Remark 1.1.

The genus 00 case of Theorem A was essentially proved by Harbater and Schneps in [13] and Hoshi, Minamide and Mochizuki in [16] (cf. Proposition 3.8). The case (g,n)=(1,2)(g,n)=(1,2) by Minamide and Nakamura in [24] (cf. Proposition 3.9).

The proof of Theorem A consists of two steps. In the first one, for SS and S′S^{\prime} hyperbolic surfaces such that g⁡(S)≥g⁡(S′)g(S)\geq g(S^{\prime}) and χ⁡(S)≤χ⁡(S′)<0\chi(S)\leq\chi(S^{\prime})<0, we construct a natural homomorphism

μS,S′:Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S′))\mu_{S,S^{\prime}}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S^{\prime}))

and we show that, essentially as a consequence of the theory developed in [7] and [8], μS,S′\mu_{S,S^{\prime}} is injective. In particular, by the genus 00 case of the theorem, we get a natural monomorphism:

μS:Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))↪GT^.\mu_{S}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\hookrightarrow\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}.

The second step then consists in showing that there is a natural (i.e. compatible with the homomorphism μS\mu_{S}) homomorphism ΨS:GT^→Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))\Psi_{S}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)). In order to construct this homomorphism, we first prove what is, in its own right, one of the main results of the paper (cf. Theorem 6.7 for a stronger statement):

Theorem B.

For a hyperbolic surface SS such that d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, there is a natural faithful representation:

ρ^GT^:GT^↪Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S)),\hat{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)),

where Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)) is the group of outer automorphisms of P​Γ^​(S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) which preserve the conjugacy class of the procyclic subgroup generated by a nonseparating Dehn twist.

The proof of Theorem B can also be split in two steps. In the first one, we use the theory of profinite hyperelliptic mapping class groups to reduce the cases of genus ≤2\leq 2 to those of genus 00 (cf. Section 6.5 to Section 6.11). In the second step, thanks to a profinite version (cf. Corollary 6.15) of a presentation given by Gervais in [11] for pure mapping class groups, we are able to extend the GT^\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}-action on profinite pure mapping class groups from genus ≤2\leq 2 to higher genus. The representation ΨS\Psi_{S} is obtained observing that the representation ρ^GT^\hat{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}} preserves the congruence kernel and then composing with the natural homomorphism Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) obtained in Theorem 4.1.

A preliminary announcement of related results appeared in [21] (cf. (ii) Théorème Principal), with a more complete treatment given recently in [22]. Previous versions of the present work predate these new developments.

1.1. Applications to Grothendieck-Teichmüller theory

A primary source of interest in the outer automorphism groups of profinite mapping class groups comes from the observation, made by Grothendieck in [12, Esquisse d’un Programme], that, by Belyǐ theorem, they contain a copy of the absolute Galois group of the rationals GℚG_{\mathbb{Q}}.

Grothendieck suggested that the étale fundamental groups of the moduli stacks P​ℳ​(S)\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S) should be assembled together in what he called the Teichmüller tower and that the automorphism group of this tower should be already determined by its truncation at modular dimension 22. He did not give many details on how to proceed in what was and remained the sketch of a research plan. It was not even clear what should be done with this automorphism group but a reasonable guess is that he hoped that it would provide a combinatorial description of the absolute Galois group GℚG_{\mathbb{Q}} (cf. Conjecture 2.10).

In the paper [9], Drinfeld initiated the study of the genus 00 stage of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower and, to this end, he introduced the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group GT^\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}. From the point of view which is relevant here, this can be described as the group of automorphisms of the first two levels (modular dimensions 11 and 22) of the genus 00 stage of the Teichmüller tower which respect a suitable inertia condition (cf. [13]).

Drinfeld then speculated, following Grothendieck, that GT^\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} should be the automorphism group of the Teichmüller tower sketched by Grothendieck but he did not give many details on how the tower should, in a precise way, be defined and such statement proved. In this paper, we will adopt the definition of the Teichmüller tower (cf. Section 2.8) proposed by Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps in [14].

The study of the genus 00 case was essentially completed by Harbater and Schneps (cf. [13, Main Theorem]). As already mentioned above, more recently, Hoshi, Minamide and Mochizuki have improved their result by showing that the inertia condition is in fact automatically satisfied (cf. [16, Corollary C]).

Theorem A and B apply, in particular, to the study of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower. For the precise definition of the profinite and the procongruence Grothendieck-Teichmüller towers 𝔗^out\hat{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}} and 𝔗ˇout\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}, we refer the reader to Section 2.8. Here it suffices to say that, in order to get enough morphisms between objects, it is necessary to consider also relative mapping class groups of surfaces with boundary. An almost immediate consequence of the general version of Theorem A (cf. Theorem 6.1) is then the procongruence version of the Drinfeld-Grothendieck conjecture:

Theorem C.

There is a natural isomorphism GT^≅Aut⁡(𝔗ˇout)\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\cong\operatorname{Aut}(\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}).

From the stronger version of Theorem B which we prove (cf. Theorem 6.7), it also follows that there is a natural faithful representation (cf. Corollary 6.24):

ρ^GT^:GT^↪Aut⁡(𝔗^out).\hat{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(\hat{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}).

This last result shows, in particular, that, even if the congruence subgroup problem had a negative answer, there are no extra restrictions on Galois actions coming from the profinite rather than the procongruence Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower.

2. Notations, definitions and preliminary results

2.1. Surfaces

In this paper, a hyperbolic surface is a connected orientable differentiable surface of negative Euler characteristic. We denote by S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} a closed oriented surface of genus g⁡(S)=gg(S)=g from which n⁡(S)=nn(S)=n points and k⁡(S)=kk(S)=k open discs have been removed. The modular dimension of SS is defined to be d⁡(S):=3​g−3+n+kd(S):=3g-3+n+k.

For k=0k=0 (resp. n=0n=0), we let Sg,n:=Sg,n0S_{g,n}:=S_{g,n}^{0} (resp. Sgk:=Sg,0kS_{g}^{k}:=S_{g,0}^{k}). Also, we let Sg:=Sg,0S_{g}:=S_{g,0}. The boundary of SS is denoted by ∂S{\partial S} and we let S̊:=S∖∂S\ring{S}:=S\smallsetminus{\partial S}, so that S̊≅Sg,n+k\ring{S}\cong S_{g,n+k}.

Let then 𝒮{\mathcal{S}} be the category with objects hyperbolic surfaces and maps embeddings of surfaces S↪S′S\hookrightarrow S^{\prime} such that a 11-punctured disc of SS is mapped either to another 11-punctured disc or to a closed disc.

2.2. Profinite and procongruence mapping class groups

For S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} a hyperbolic surface, we let Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) and P​Γ​(S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S) be respectively the mapping class group and the pure mapping class group associated to SS. Note that the inclusion S̊↪S\ring{S}\hookrightarrow S induces, by restriction, a natural homomorphism Γ⁡(S)↪Γ⁡(S̊){\Gamma}(S)\hookrightarrow{\Gamma}(\ring{S}) whose image is the stabilizer of the partition of the punctures of S̊\ring{S} into those which have a boundary in SS and those which do not.

For S=Sg,nS=S_{g,n}, sometimes, to simplify notation, we will denote the corresponding mapping and pure mapping class groups by Γg,[n]{\Gamma}_{g,[n]} and Γg,n{\Gamma}_{g,n}, respectively. These groups are then related by the short exact sequence 1→P​Γ​(S)→Γ⁡(S)→Σn→11\to{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S)\to{\Gamma}(S)\to\Sigma_{n}\to 1, where Σn\Sigma_{n} is the symmetric group on nn letters.

The profinite and the pure profinite mapping class groups Γ^​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) and P​Γ^​(S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) are defined to be the profinite completions of the groups Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) and P​Γ​(S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S), respectively.

Let Π\Pi be the fundamental group of the surface SS with respect to some base point and let Π^{\widehat{\Pi}} be its profinite completion. Since Π\Pi is conjugacy separable and class automorphisms of Π\Pi are inner, the group Out⁡(Π)\operatorname{Out}(\Pi) naturally embeds in Out⁡(Π^)\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Pi}}). Moreover, since (topologically) finitely generated profinite groups are strongly complete, Out⁡(Π^)\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Pi}}) is a profinite group.

Therefore, both groups Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) and P​Γ​(S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S) naturally embed in the profinite group Out⁡(Π^)\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Pi}}) and inherit a profinite topology which is called the congruence topology. The completions of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) and P​Γ​(S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S) with respect to these topologies are denoted by Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) and P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) and called the procongruence and the pure procongruence mapping class group, respectively. For surfaces with empty boundary, these groups are studied in detail in [3] and [5]. In what follows, we will recall the basic properties we need and prove a few more for surfaces with boundary.

2.3. The congruence subgroup problem

The congruence subgroup problem asks if there is an isomorphism Γ^​(S)≅Γˇ​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)\cong{\check{\Gamma}}(S) (equiv. P​Γ^​(S)≅P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)\cong{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)). This is known to be true only for g⁡(S)≤2g(S)\leq 2 (cf. [1], [2] and [5]). In the sequel, we will identify the profinite and the procongruence mapping class groups for g⁡(S)≤2g(S)\leq 2.

2.4. Profinite Dehn twists and profinite braid twists

Let ℒ⁡(S){\mathcal{L}}(S) be the set of isotopy classes of simple closed curves on SS. We then denote by ℒ​(S)0{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0} the subset of ℒ⁡(S){\mathcal{L}}(S) consisting of nonperipheral curves. The set ℒ​(S)0{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0} parameterizes the set of Dehn twists in Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) (cf. [10, Section 3.1.1] for the definition). For γ∈ℒ​(S)0{\gamma}\in{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0}, we denote by τγ∈P​Γ​(S)⊆Γ⁡(S)\tau_{\gamma}\in{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S)\subseteq{\Gamma}(S) the associated Dehn twist.

Let us denote by ℒb​(S){\mathcal{L}}^{b}(S) the subset of ℒ⁡(S){\mathcal{L}}(S) consisting of simple closed curves bounding a 22-punctured disc on SS. For γ∈ℒb​(S){\gamma}\in{\mathcal{L}}^{b}(S), let DD be the disc bounded by γ{\gamma}. Then, the braid twist bγb_{\gamma} about γ{\gamma} is the isotopy class of a self-homeomorphism of SS which is the identity outside of DD, swaps the punctures of BB and satisfies the identity bγ2=τγb_{\gamma}^{2}=\tau_{\gamma}.

The mapping class groups P​Γ​(S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S) and Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) are generated, respectively, by Dehn twists and by Dehn twists and braid twists (cf. [10, Corollary 4.15]).

A profinite Dehn twist (resp. profinite braid twist) of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) is an element which lies in the closure of the set of Dehn twists (resp. braid twists) inside the profinite group Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) (where we identify Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) with a subgroup of the latter group).

It is a remarkable and nontrivial fact that the profinite Dehn twists of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) are parameterized by the profinite set of nonperipheral profinite simple closed curves ℒ^​(S)0\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0} (cf. [3, Theorem 5.1]). This set is realized, roughly speaking, as the closure of ℒ​(S)0{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0} inside the profinite set of ”unoriented” conjugacy classes in Π^{\widehat{\Pi}} (cf. [3, Section 4] and [5, Section 3.2] for the precise definition). As above, we then denote by τγ∈P​Γˇ​(S)\tau_{\gamma}\in{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S), for γ∈ℒ^​(S)0{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0}, the associated profinite Dehn twist.

Let ℒ^b​(S)\widehat{\mathcal{L}}^{b}(S) be the subset of ℒ^​(S)\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S) consisting of profinite simple closed curves whose topological type (cf. [7, Definition 4.7]) is that of a simple closed curve bounding a 22-punctured disc. Then, the the profinite braid twists of the procongruence mapping class group Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) are parameterized by this profinite set and are denoted by bγb_{\gamma}, for γ∈ℒ^b​(S){\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}^{b}(S).

2.5. Multicurves and their stabilizers

A multicurve σ{\sigma} on SS is a set of isotopy classes of disjoint simple closed curves on SS such that S∖σS\smallsetminus{\sigma} does not contain a disc or a one-punctured disc. The topological type of σ{\sigma} is the topological type of the surface S∖σS\smallsetminus{\sigma}. Multicurves parameterize sets of commuting Dehn twists or braid twists in Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S). The complex of curves C⁡(S)C(S) is the abstract simplicial complex whose simplices are multicurves on SS. Its combinatorial dimension is d⁡(S)−1d(S)-1.

Definition 2.1.

For σ∈C⁡(S){\sigma}\in C(S), we denote by IσI_{\sigma} the abelian subgroup of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) generated by the Dehn twists τγ\tau_{\gamma}, for γ∈σ{\gamma}\in{\sigma}. For HH a subgroup of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S), we then let Iσ​(H):=Iσ∩HI_{\sigma}(H):=I_{\sigma}\cap H. The topological type of IσI_{\sigma} is the topological type of σ{\sigma}.

There is a natural simplicial action of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) on C⁡(S)C(S). Let us describe the stabilizer of a simplex σ∈C⁡(S){\sigma}\in C(S). Let S∖σ=S1​∐…​∐SkS\smallsetminus{\sigma}=S_{1}\coprod\ldots\coprod S_{k}, let BiB_{i} be the set of punctures of SiS_{i} bounded by a curve in σ{\sigma}, for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k, and let Σσ±\Sigma_{{\sigma}^{\pm}} be the symmetric group on the set of oriented circles σ±:=σ+∪σ−{\sigma}^{\pm}:={\sigma}^{+}\cup{\sigma}^{-}. Let us also denote by Γ​(Si)Bi{\Gamma}(S_{i})_{B_{i}} the pointwise stabilizer of the subset of punctures BiB_{i} for the action of the mapping class group Γ⁡(Si){\Gamma}(S_{i}), for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k. Then, the stabilizer Γ​(S)σ{\Gamma}(S)_{\sigma} is described by the two exact sequences:

1→Γ​(S)σ→→Γ​(S)σ→Σσ±,1→Iσ→Γ​(S)σ→→Γ​(S1)B1×…×Γ​(Sk)Bk→1.\begin{array}[]{c}1\to{\Gamma}(S)_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\Gamma}(S)_{\sigma}\to\Sigma_{{\sigma}^{\pm}},\\ \\ 1\to I_{\sigma}\to{\Gamma}(S)_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\Gamma}(S_{1})_{B_{1}}\times\ldots\times{\Gamma}(S_{k})_{B_{k}}\to 1.\end{array}

A similar description but simpler applies to the stabilizer P​Γ​(S)σ{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S)_{\sigma} for the action of the pure mapping class group P​Γ​(S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S) on C⁡(S)C(S):

1→P​Γ​(S)σ→→P​Γ​(S)σ→Σσ±,1→Iσ→P​Γ​(S)σ→→P​Γ​(S1)×…×P​Γ​(Sk)→1.\begin{array}[]{c}1\to{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S)_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S)_{\sigma}\to\Sigma_{{\sigma}^{\pm}},\\ \\ 1\to I_{\sigma}\to{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S)_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S_{1})\times\ldots\times{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S_{k})\to 1.\end{array}

2.6. The procongruence curve complex

A central object for the study of procongruence mapping class groups is a profinite version of the complex of curves. For every k≥0k\geq 0, there is a natural embedding C​(S)k↪𝒫k+1​(ℒ^​(S))C(S)_{k}\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{P}}_{k+1}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)), where 𝒫k+1​(ℒ^​(S)){\mathcal{P}}_{k+1}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)) is the profinite set of unordered subsets of k+1k+1 distinct elements in ℒ^​(S)\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S). We then define:

Definition 2.2.

The procongruence curve complex (or complex of profinite curves) Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) (cf. [3, Section 4], for more details) is the abstract simplicial profinite complex whose set Cˇ​(S)k{\check{C}}(S)_{k} of kk-simplices is the closure of C​(S)kC(S)_{k} inside 𝒫k+1​(ℒ^​(S)){\mathcal{P}}_{k+1}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)). In particular, Cˇ​(S)0=ℒ^​(S)0{\check{C}}(S)_{0}=\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0}. A simplex σ{\sigma} of Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) is also called a profinite multicurve. Its topological type is the topological type of a simplex in the intersection of the orbit Γˇ​(S)⋅σ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\cdot{\sigma} with C​(S)⊂Cˇ​(S)C(S)\subset{\check{C}}(S).

There are continuous natural actions of the procongruence mapping class groups Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) and P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) on Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S). [3, Theorem 4.5] describes the stabilizers for the action of P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S). This result implies a similar description for the action of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) (cf. [7, Theorem 4.10]):

Theorem 2.3.

For σ∈C​(S)⊂Cˇ​(S){\sigma}\in C(S)\subset{\check{C}}(S), let S∖σ=S1​∐…​∐SkS\smallsetminus{\sigma}=S_{1}\coprod\ldots\coprod S_{k} and BiB_{i} be the set of punctures of SiS_{i} bounded by a curve in σ{\sigma}, for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k. Then, we have:

  1. (i)

    The stabilizer Γˇ​(S)σ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\sigma} is described by the two exact sequences:

    1→Γˇ​(S)σ→→Γˇ​(S)σ→Σσ±,1→I^σ→Γˇ​(S)σ→→Γˇ​(S1)B1×…×Γˇ​(Sk)Bk→1,\begin{array}[]{c}1\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\sigma}\to\Sigma_{{\sigma}^{\pm}},\\ \\ 1\to{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S_{1})_{B_{1}}\times\ldots\times{\check{\Gamma}}(S_{k})_{B_{k}}\to 1,\end{array}

    where I^σ{\hat{I}}_{\sigma} is the profinite completion of the free abelian group IσI_{\sigma} and Γˇ​(Si)Bi{\check{\Gamma}}(S_{i})_{B_{i}} is the pointwise stabilizer of the subset of punctures BiB_{i} in Γˇ​(Si){\check{\Gamma}}(S_{i}), for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k.

  2. (ii)

    The stabilizer P​Γˇ​(S)σ{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\sigma} is described by the two exact sequences:

    1→P​Γˇ​(S)σ→→P​Γˇ​(S)σ→Σσ±,1→I^σ→P​Γˇ​(S)σ→→P​Γˇ​(S1)×…×P​Γˇ​(Sk)→1.\begin{array}[]{c}1\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\sigma}\to\Sigma_{{\sigma}^{\pm}},\\ \\ 1\to{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S_{1})\times\ldots\times{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S_{k})\to 1.\end{array}

2.7. Profinite and procongruence relative mapping class groups

For a hyperbolic surface S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k}, we let Γ⁡(S,∂S){\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}) be the relative mapping class group of the surface with boundary (S,∂S)(S,{\partial S}), that is to say the group of relative, with respect to the boundary ∂S{\partial S}, isotopy classes of orientation preserving diffeomorphisms of SS. Let δ1,…,δk\delta_{1},\ldots,\delta_{k} be the connected components of the boundary ∂S{\partial S}. Then, the group Γ⁡(S,∂S){\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}) is described by the natural short exact sequence:

1→∏i=1kτδiℤ→Γ⁡(S,∂S)→Γ⁡(S)→1.1\to\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\mathbb{Z}}\to{\Gamma}(S,{\partial S})\to{\Gamma}(S)\to 1.

The relative pure mapping class group P​Γ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}) is the subgroup of Γ⁡(S,∂S){\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}) consisting of those elements which admit representatives fixing pointwise the punctures and the boundary of SS. It is described by the short exact sequence:

1→P​Γ​(S,∂S)→Γ⁡(S,∂S)→Σn×Σk→1.1\to{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S,{\partial S})\to{\Gamma}(S,{\partial S})\to\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}\to 1.
Remark 2.4.

Let S~=Sg,n+2​k{\widetilde{S}}=S_{g,n+2k}, with d⁡(S~)>1d({\widetilde{S}})>1 and σ={δ1,…,δk}∈C⁡(S~){\sigma}=\{\delta_{1},\ldots,\delta_{k}\}\in C({\widetilde{S}}), where δi\delta_{i} is a simple closed curve bounding an open disc DiD_{i} containing the punctures indexed by n+2​i−1n+2i-1 and n+2​in+2i, for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k. Let S:=S~∖∪i=1kDi≅Sg,nkS:={\widetilde{S}}\smallsetminus\cup_{i=1}^{k}D_{i}\cong S_{g,n}^{k}. The relative mapping class group Γ⁡(S,∂S){\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}) then identifies with a subgroup of the stabilizer Γ​(S~)σ{\Gamma}({\widetilde{S}})_{\sigma}, which is described by the short exact sequence:

1→∏i=1kτδiℤ→Γ​(S~)σ→(Σ2)k⋊Γ⁡(S)→1,1\to\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\mathbb{Z}}\to{\Gamma}({\widetilde{S}})_{\sigma}\to(\Sigma_{2})^{k}\rtimes{\Gamma}(S)\to 1,

where Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) acts on the product (Σ2)k(\Sigma_{2})^{k} by permuting its factors through the natural representation Γ⁡(S)→Σk{\Gamma}(S)\to\Sigma_{k}. There is also a natural isomorphism P​Γ​(S,∂S)≅P​Γ​(S~)σ→{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S,{\partial S})\cong{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}({\widetilde{S}})_{\vec{\sigma}}.

The profinite (resp. profinite pure) relative mapping class group of the surface with boundary (S,∂S)(S,{\partial S}) is defined to be the profinite completion Γ^​(S,∂S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) (resp. P​Γ^​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) of Γ⁡(S,∂S){\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}) (resp. of P​Γ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S,{\partial S})). From (ii) of Theorem 2.3 and Remark 2.4, it follows that these profinite groups are described by the short exact sequences:

(1) 1→∏i=1kτδiℤ^→Γ^​(S,∂S)→Γ^​(S)→1and 1→P​Γ^​(S,∂S)→Γ^​(S,∂S)→Σn×Σk→1.\begin{array}[]{ll}&1\to\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}\to{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)\to 1\\ \mbox{and }&\\ &1\to{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}\to 1.\end{array}
Definition 2.5.

For a surface S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} with boundary ∂S=∪i=1kδi{\partial S}=\cup_{i=1}^{k}\delta_{i}, we let S~≅Sg,n+2​k{\widetilde{S}}\cong S_{g,n+2k} be the surface obtained from SS glueing a 22-punctured disc over each boundary component δi\delta_{i}, for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k.

By Remark 2.4, the embedding S↪S~S\hookrightarrow{\widetilde{S}} induces a monomorphism of mapping class groups Γ⁡(S,∂S)↪Γ⁡(S~){\Gamma}(S,{\partial S})\hookrightarrow{\Gamma}({\widetilde{S}}), which identifies Γ⁡(S,∂S){\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}) with a subgroup of the stabilizer Γ​(S~)σ{\Gamma}({\widetilde{S}})_{\sigma}.

The congruence topology on Γ⁡(S~){\Gamma}({\widetilde{S}}) then induces a profinite topology on Γ⁡(S,∂S){\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}) which we call the congruence topology on Γ⁡(S,∂S){\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}). This clearly also defines a profinite topology on P​Γ​(S,∂S)⊆Γ⁡(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S,{\partial S})\subseteq{\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}), which we call the congruence topology on P​Γ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}).

The completions of Γ⁡(S,∂S){\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}) and P​Γ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}) with respect to these congruence topologies are then denoted by Γˇ​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) and P​Γˇ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}), respectively, and are called the procongruence (resp. pure) relative mapping class group of the surface with boundary (S,∂S)(S,{\partial S}).

By Theorem 2.3, they fit in the short exact sequences:

(2) 1→∏i=1kτδiℤ^→Γˇ​(S,∂S)→Γˇ​(S)→1and 1→P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)→Γˇ​(S,∂S)→Σn×Σk→1.\begin{array}[]{ll}&1\to\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\to 1\\ \mbox{and }&\\ &1\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}\to 1.\end{array}

An immediate consequence is then:

Proposition 2.6.
  1. (i)

    For g⁡(S)≤2g(S)\leq 2, we have Γˇ​(S,∂S)=Γ^​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})={\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) and P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)=P​Γ^​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})={\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}).

  2. (ii)

    For S≠S2,S1,2S\neq S_{2},S_{1,2} and S12S_{1}^{2}, we have Z⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))=(∏i=1kτδi)ℤ^Z({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))=(\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}})^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}. Otherwise, the center Z​(Γˇ​(S,∂S))Z({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) is generated by (∏i=1kτδi)ℤ^(\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}})^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} and the hyperelliptic involution.

  3. (iii)

    For S≠S2,S1,2,S12S\neq S_{2},S_{1,2},S_{1}^{2} and UU an open subgroup of P​Γˇ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}), we have ZΓˇ​(S,∂S)​(U)=∏i=1kτδiℤ^Z_{{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})}(U)=\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}. Otherwise, ZΓˇ​(S,∂S)​(U)Z_{{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})}(U) is generated by ∏i=1kτδiℤ^\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} and the hyperelliptic involution.

Proof.

The first item follows from the congruence subgroup property in genus ≤2\leq 2 for surfaces without boundary and the short exact sequences (1) and (2). The second and the third item from the same exact sequences, [3, Corollary 6.2] and [7, Theorem 4.14]. ∎

The procongruence (resp. pure) relative mapping class group Γˇ​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) (resp. P​Γˇ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) acts on the procongruence curve complex Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) through the natural homomorphism to Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) (resp. P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)). For σ∈C⁡(S){\sigma}\in C(S), let IσI_{\sigma} be the subgroup of Γ⁡(S,∂S){\Gamma}(S,{\partial S}) generated by the Dehn twists τγ\tau_{\gamma}, for γ∈σ{\gamma}\in{\sigma} (cf. Definition 2.1). Then, from Theorem 2.3, it easily follows:

Theorem 2.7.

For σ∈C​(S)⊂Cˇ​(S){\sigma}\in C(S)\subset{\check{C}}(S), let S∖σ=S1​∐…​∐SkS\smallsetminus{\sigma}=S_{1}\coprod\ldots\coprod S_{k} and BiB_{i} be the set of punctures of SiS_{i} bounded by a curve in σ{\sigma}, for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k. Then, we have:

  1. (i)

    The stabilizer Γˇ​(S,∂S)σ{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\sigma} is described by the two exact sequences:

    1→Γˇ​(S,∂S)σ→→Γˇ​(S,∂S)σ→Σσ±,1→I^σ→Γˇ(S,∂S)σ→→Γˇ(S1,∂S1)B1×…×Γˇ(Sk,,∂Sk)Bk→1,\begin{array}[]{c}1\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\sigma}\to\Sigma_{{\sigma}^{\pm}},\\ \\ 1\to{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S_{1},{\partial S}_{1})_{B_{1}}\times\ldots\times{\check{\Gamma}}(S_{k},,{\partial S}_{k})_{B_{k}}\to 1,\end{array}

    where I^σ{\hat{I}}_{\sigma} is the profinite completion of the free abelian group IσI_{\sigma} and Γˇ(Si,,∂Si)Bi{\check{\Gamma}}(S_{i},,{\partial S}_{i})_{B_{i}} is the pointwise stabilizer of the subset of punctures BiB_{i} in Γˇ(Si,,∂Si){\check{\Gamma}}(S_{i},,{\partial S}_{i}), for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k.

  2. (ii)

    The stabilizer P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)σ{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\sigma} is described by the two exact sequences:

    1→P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)σ→→P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)σ→Σσ±,1→I^σ→P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)σ→→P​Γˇ​(S1,∂S1)×…×P​Γˇ​(Sk,∂Sk)→1.\begin{array}[]{c}1\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\sigma}\to\Sigma_{{\sigma}^{\pm}},\\ \\ 1\to{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S_{1},{\partial S}_{1})\times\ldots\times{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S_{k},{\partial S}_{k})\to 1.\end{array}

From the definition of the congruence topology and [7, Corollary 4.12], it then follows a description of the centralizers of profinite multitwists in procongruence relative mapping class groups:

Theorem 2.8.

For σ={γ0,…,γk}{\sigma}=\{{\gamma}_{0},\ldots,{\gamma}_{k}\} a profinite multicurve on SS and m∈ℤ∖{0}m\in\mathbb{Z}\smallsetminus\{0\}, we have:

ZΓˇ​(S,∂S)(τγ0m⋯τγkm)=NΓˇ​(S,∂S)((τγ0m⋯τγkm)ℤ^)=NΓˇ​(S,∂S)(⟨τγ0m,…,τγkm⟩)=Γˇ(S,∂S)σ,Z_{{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})}(\tau_{{\gamma}_{0}}^{m}\cdots\tau_{{\gamma}_{k}}^{m})=N_{{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})}((\tau_{{\gamma}_{0}}^{m}\cdots\tau_{{\gamma}_{k}}^{m})^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}})=N_{{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})}(\langle\tau_{{\gamma}_{0}}^{m},\ldots,\tau_{{\gamma}_{k}}^{m}\rangle)={\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\sigma},

where Γˇ​(S,∂S)σ{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\sigma} is the stabilizer of σ{\sigma} described in (i) of Theorem 2.7. A similar result holds for the procongruence pure relative mapping class group P​Γˇ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}).

2.8. The Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower

Let η:S↪S′\eta\colon\thinspace S\hookrightarrow S^{\prime} be a map in the category of surfaces 𝒮{\mathcal{S}} defined in Section 2.1. Then, η\eta induces a homomorphism of pure relative mapping class groups η∗:P​Γ​(S,∂S)→P​Γ​(S′,∂S′)\eta_{\ast}\colon\thinspace{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S,{\partial S})\to{\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S^{\prime},{\partial S}^{\prime}) and hence of profinite pure relative mapping class groups η^∗:P​Γ^​(S,∂S)→P​Γ^​(S′,∂S′)\hat{\eta}_{\ast}\colon\thinspace{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S^{\prime},{\partial S}^{\prime}). From Remark 2.4 and (ii) of Theorem 2.3, it follows that η^∗\hat{\eta}_{\ast} also induces a homomorphism of procongruence pure relative mapping class groups ηˇ∗:P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)→P​Γˇ​(S′,∂S′)\check{\eta}_{\ast}\colon\thinspace{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S^{\prime},{\partial S}^{\prime}).

Let 𝒢{\mathcal{G}} be the category of profinite groups and continuous homomorphisms. We have then defined two functors 𝔗^\hat{\mathfrak{T}} and 𝔗ˇ\check{\mathfrak{T}} from 𝒮{\mathcal{S}} to 𝒢{\mathcal{G}}. It is not difficult to see that the functor 𝔗ˇ\check{\mathfrak{T}} factors through the functor 𝔗^\hat{\mathfrak{T}}.

There is a natural way to realize the above profinite mapping class groups as geometric étale fundamental groups of suitable geometric objects. We will associate to a hyperbolic surface SS a logarithmic formal DM stack P​ℳ​(S)\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S) (cf. [28] for a similar construction).

For a surface SS with empty boundary, let P​ℳ​(S)\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S) be the DM stack of smooth curves whose complex model is diffeomorphic to SS with an order on the set of punctures and let P​ℳ¯​(S)\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S) be the DM compactification of P​ℳ​(S)\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S). Let then P​ℳ¯​(S)log\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S)^{\log} be the log DM stack with the logarithmic structure associated to the DM boundary. There is a natural fully faithful functor from the category of DM stacks to the category of formal DM stacks. We then denote by P​ℳ¯​(S,∅)log\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S,\emptyset)^{\log} the formal log DM stack associated to the log DM stack P​ℳ¯​(S)log\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S)^{\log} and assign this to the surface SS. There is a series of isomorphisms:

π1et​(P​ℳ¯​(S,∅)ℚ¯log)≅π1et​(P​ℳ¯​(S)ℚ¯log)≅π1et​(P​ℳ​(S)ℚ¯)≅P​Γ^​(S).\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S,\emptyset)^{\log}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}})\cong\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S)^{\log}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}})\cong\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}})\cong{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S).

For a surface SS with nonempty boundary, let S~≅Sg,n+2​k{\widetilde{S}}\cong S_{g,n+2k} be as in Definition 2.5. The simplex σ={δ1,…,δk}∈C⁡(S~){\sigma}=\{\delta_{1},\ldots,\delta_{k}\}\in C({\widetilde{S}}) determines a closed stratum δσ\delta_{\sigma} in the boundary of P​ℳ¯​(S~)\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}({\widetilde{S}}) and we let P​ℳ​(S,∂S)\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S,{\partial S}) be the normalization of a formal neighborhood of δσ\delta_{\sigma} in P​ℳ¯​(S~)\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}({\widetilde{S}}).

Let us then assign to SS the formal logarithmic DM stack P​ℳ​(S,∂S)log\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S,{\partial S})^{\log} obtained by pulling back to the formal DM stack P​ℳ​(S,∂S)\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S,{\partial S}) the logarithmic structure of P​ℳ¯​(S~,∅)log\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}({\widetilde{S}},\emptyset)^{\log}, via the natural morphism of formal DM stacks P​ℳ​(S,∂S)→P​ℳ​(S~,∅)\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S,{\partial S})\to\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}({\widetilde{S}},\emptyset). There is an isomorphism:

π1et​(P​ℳ¯​(S,∂S)ℚ¯log)≅P​Γ^​(S,∂S).\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S,{\partial S})^{\log}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}})\cong{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}).

From the canonical short exact sequence

1→π1et​(P​ℳ¯​(S,∂S)ℚ¯log)→π1et​(P​ℳ¯​(S,∂S)ℚlog)→Gℚ→1,1\to\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S,{\partial S})^{\log}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}})\to\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S,{\partial S})^{\log}_{\mathbb{Q}})\to G_{\mathbb{Q}}\to 1,

we get a natural outer representation ρ^S:Gℚ→Out⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S))\hat{\rho}_{S}\colon\thinspace G_{\mathbb{Q}}\to\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})). A (nontrivial) consequence of Belyǐ theorem is that this representation is faithful.

The Grothendieck-Teichmüller functor 𝔗^\hat{\mathfrak{T}} factors as the composition of the functor P​ℳ¯ℚlog\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}^{\log}_{\mathbb{Q}}, which assigns to the surface SS the log formal DM stack P​ℳ¯​(S,∂S)ℚlog\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S,{\partial S})^{\log}_{\mathbb{Q}}, and the functor which assigns to a log formal DM stack XlogX^{\log} over the rationals its geometric étale fundamental group π1et​(Xℚ¯log)\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(X_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}^{\log}).

Note that the identification of topological fundamental groups with mapping class groups takes care of base points. However, in order to make keeping track of base points totally irrelevant, it is convenient to modify our definition of the functors 𝔗^\hat{\mathfrak{T}} and 𝔗ˇ\check{\mathfrak{T}}. Let 𝒢out{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathrm{out}} be the category with objects profinite groups and maps outer continuous homomorphisms. There is a natural functor 𝒢→𝒢out{\mathcal{G}}\to{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathrm{out}} and we define 𝔗^out\hat{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}} and 𝔗ˇout\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}} to be, respectively, the composition of 𝔗^\hat{\mathfrak{T}} and 𝔗ˇ\check{\mathfrak{T}} with this functor.

Definition 2.9.

The full images in 𝒢out{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathrm{out}} of the functors 𝔗^out\hat{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}} and 𝔗ˇout\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}} are called the (profinite) Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower and the procongruence Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower, respectively.

From the geometric description of the functor 𝔗^out\hat{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}, it follows that there is a natural faithful representation:

ρ𝔗^:Gℚ↪Aut⁡(𝔗^out),\rho_{\hat{\mathfrak{T}}}\colon\thinspace G_{\mathbb{Q}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(\hat{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}),

defined by the assignment α↦{ρ^S​(α)}S∈𝒮\alpha\mapsto\{\hat{\rho}_{S}(\alpha)\}_{S\in{\mathcal{S}}}. At the heart of Grothendieck-Teichmüller theory, is the following apocryphal conjecture by Grothendieck:

Conjecture 2.10 (Grothendieck).

The representation ρ𝔗^\rho_{\hat{\mathfrak{T}}} induces a natural isomorphism:

Gℚ≅Aut⁡(𝔗^out).G_{\mathbb{Q}}\cong\operatorname{Aut}(\hat{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}).

Somewhat in this spirit is the I/OM conjecture, proved by Pop (cf. [25, Theorem]).

2.9. The Galois action on the procongruence Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower

For SS a hyperbolic surface with empty boundary, let P​𝒞¯​(S)log→P​ℳ¯​(S)log\mathrm{P}{\overline{{\mathscr{C}}}}(S)^{\log}\to\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S)^{\log} be the universal log stable curve (this is the universal stable curve endowed with the logarithmic structure associated to its DM boundary). For ξ¯∈P​ℳ¯​(S)log\bar{\xi}\in\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S)^{\log} a ℚ¯\overline{\mathbb{Q}}-point, there is an associated universal monodromy representation:

ρξ¯:π1et​(P​ℳ¯​(S)ℚ¯log)→Out⁡(P​𝒞¯​(S)ξ¯log),\rho_{\bar{\xi}}\colon\thinspace\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S)^{\log}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}})\to\operatorname{Out}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{{\mathscr{C}}}}(S)^{\log}_{\bar{\xi}}),

where P​𝒞¯​(S)ξ¯log\mathrm{P}{\overline{{\mathscr{C}}}}(S)^{\log}_{\bar{\xi}} is the fiber of the universal curve over ξ¯\bar{\xi} endowed with the logarithmic structure induced by P​𝒞¯​(S)log\mathrm{P}{\overline{{\mathscr{C}}}}(S)^{\log}. The isomorphism π1et​(P​ℳ¯​(S)ℚ¯log)≅P​Γ^​(S)\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S)^{\log}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}})\cong{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) then induces an isomorphism Im⁡ρξ¯≅P​Γˇ​(S)\operatorname{Im}\rho_{\bar{\xi}}\cong{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S).

For ψ:S↪S~\psi\colon\thinspace S\hookrightarrow{\widetilde{S}} the embedding considered in Remark 2.4, there is an induced homomorphism:

𝔗^​(ψ):π1et​(P​ℳ¯​(S,∂S)ℚ¯log)≅P​Γ^​(S,∂S)→π1et​(P​ℳ¯​(S~,∅)ℚ¯log)≅π1et​(P​ℳ¯​(S~)ℚ¯log).\hat{\mathfrak{T}}(\psi)\colon\thinspace\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S,{\partial S})^{\log}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}})\cong{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}({\widetilde{S}},\emptyset)^{\log}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}})\cong\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}({\widetilde{S}})^{\log}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}).

We then have ρξ¯∘𝔗^​(ψ)​(π1et​(P​ℳ¯​(S,∂S)ℚ¯log))≅P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)\rho_{\bar{\xi}}\circ\hat{\mathfrak{T}}(\psi)(\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S,{\partial S})^{\log}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}))\cong{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}).

The above procedure defines natural transformations of functors:

ρ:𝔗^⇒𝔗ˇandρout:𝔗^out⇒𝔗ˇout.\rho\colon\thinspace\hat{\mathfrak{T}}\Rightarrow\check{\mathfrak{T}}\hskip 28.45274pt\mbox{and}\hskip 28.45274pt\rho^{\mathrm{out}}\colon\thinspace\hat{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}\Rightarrow\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}.

Since the universal monodromy representation ρξ¯\rho_{\bar{\xi}} is compatible with the Galois actions, the natural transformation ρout\rho^{\mathrm{out}} is GℚG_{\mathbb{Q}}-equivariant and there is a natural representation (again, Belyǐ theorem implies that it is faithful):

ρ𝔗ˇ:Gℚ↪Aut⁡(𝔗ˇout).\rho_{\check{\mathfrak{T}}}\colon\thinspace G_{\mathbb{Q}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}).

2.10. Levels and level structures

Let SS be a hyperbolic surface with empty boundary. A finite index subgroup Γλ{\Gamma}^{\lambda} of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) is called a level. A congruence level is a level which is open for the congruence topology on Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S). The étale covering ℳλ​(S){\mathcal{M}}^{\lambda}(S) of ℳ⁡(S){\mathcal{M}}(S) associated to the level Γλ{\Gamma}^{\lambda} is called a level structure over ℳ⁡(S){\mathcal{M}}(S). The level is representable if the associated DM stack ℳλ​(S){\mathcal{M}}^{\lambda}(S) is representable.

In particular, to the pure mapping class group P​Γ​(S){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S) is associated the level structure P​ℳ​(S)\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S). This is the étale Galois covering of ℳ⁡(S){\mathcal{M}}(S), with Galois group the symmetric group Σn\Sigma_{n}, which parameterizes smooth projective curves with an order on the set of punctures. For S=Sg,nS=S_{g,n}, in order to simplify notations, the stacks ℳ⁡(S){\mathcal{M}}(S) and P​ℳ​(S)\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S) are sometimes simply denoted by ℳg,[n]{\mathcal{M}}_{g,[n]} and ℳg,n{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}, respectively.

Let ℳ¯​(S){\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S) be the DM compactification of the moduli stack ℳ⁡(S){\mathcal{M}}(S). This is a DM stack defined over ℤ\mathbb{Z} which parameterizes stable nn-punctured, genus gg curves. A level structure over ℳ¯​(S){\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S) is the compactification ℳ¯λ​(S){\overline{\mathcal{M}}}^{\lambda}(S) of a level structure ℳλ​(S){\mathcal{M}}^{\lambda}(S) over ℳ⁡(S){\mathcal{M}}(S) obtained taking the normalization of the DM stack ℳ¯​(S){\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S) in the function field of ℳλ​(S){\mathcal{M}}^{\lambda}(S). This is also a DM stack and, if the level Γλ{\Gamma}^{\lambda} is contained in an abelian level of order ≥3\geq 3, then ℳ¯λ​(S){\overline{\mathcal{M}}}^{\lambda}(S) is representable.

2.11. The procongruence pants graph

The Fulton curve ℱ⁡(S){\mathcal{F}}(S) is the 11-dimensional closed substack of the moduli stack ℳ¯​(S){\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S) which parameterizes curves with at least d−1d-1 singular points. More generally, for a level structure ℳ¯λ​(S){\overline{\mathcal{M}}}^{\lambda}(S) over ℳ¯​(S){\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S), the Fulton curve ℱλ​(S){\mathcal{F}}^{\lambda}(S) is the inverse image of ℱ⁡(S){\mathcal{F}}(S) via the natural morphism ℳ¯λ​(S)→ℳ¯​(S){\overline{\mathcal{M}}}^{\lambda}(S)\to{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S).

Let Γλ{\Gamma}^{\lambda} be a representable level of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) contained in an abelian level of order m≥2m\geq 2. Then, each irreducible component of the Fulton curve ℱλ​(S)ℚ{\mathcal{F}}^{\lambda}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}} is a covering of ℙℚ1{\mathbb{P}}^{1}_{\mathbb{Q}} ramified at most over the set {0,1,∞}\{0,1,\infty\} and the ramification points are contained in the boundary of ℱλ​(S)ℚ{\mathcal{F}}^{\lambda}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}} (that is to say the points parameterizing maximally degenerated stable curves). It follows that the analytic complex variety ℱ​(S)ℂa​n{\mathcal{F}}(S)_{\mathbb{C}}^{an} admits a natural triangulation with vertices the points parameterizing maximally degenerated stable curves and edges geodesic segments of length 11 joining these boundary points. We denote by CPλ​(S)C^{\lambda}_{P}(S) the 11-skeleton of this triangulation which we regard as a 11-dimensional abstract simplicial complex.

Definition 2.11.

The procongruence pants graph CˇP​(S){\check{C}}_{P}(S) is the 11-dimensional abstract simplicial profinite complex obtained as the inverse limit of the finite abstract simplicial complexes CPλ​(S)C^{\lambda}_{P}(S), for Γλ{\Gamma}^{\lambda} varying over the set of all congruence levels of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S).

For a more comprehensive treatment of CˇP​(S){\check{C}}_{P}(S), we refer to [7]. Here we only recall the basic properties which we will need later. The vertices of CˇP​(S){\check{C}}_{P}(S) are in natural bijective correspondence with the profinite set Cˇ​(S)d⁡(S)−1{\check{C}}(S)_{d(S)-1} of facets of the procongruence curve complex and its edges with the profinite set Cˇ​(S)d⁡(S)−2{\check{C}}(S)_{d(S)-2} of (d⁡(S)−2)(d(S)-2)-simplices. To the decomposition in irreducible components of the Fulton curves ℱλ​(S){\mathcal{F}}^{\lambda}(S), for all levels Γλ{\Gamma}^{\lambda}, corresponds a decomposition of the procongruence pants graph CˇP​(S){\check{C}}_{P}(S) in closed subgraphs called profinite Farey subgraphs. They are parameterized by the profinite set Cˇ​(S)d⁡(S)−2{\check{C}}(S)_{d(S)-2}. The profinite Farey subgraph associated to σ∈Cˇ​(S)d⁡(S)−2{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)_{d(S)-2} is denoted by F^σ​(S){\widehat{\operatorname{F}}}_{\sigma}(S) and its set of vertices consists of the profinite set of facets of CˇP​(S){\check{C}}_{P}(S) containing σ{\sigma}.

3. The 𝕀\mathbb{I}-condition and the 𝔻\mathbb{D}-condition on automorphisms

3.1. Decomposition and inertia groups

Let SS be a hyperbolic surface. For an open subgroup UU of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S), we call the stabilizer Uσ=U∩Γˇ​(S)σU_{\sigma}=U\cap{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\sigma} of a simplex σ∈Cˇ​(S){\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S) for the action of UU on Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) the decomposition group of UU associated to σ{\sigma}.

Definition 3.1.

The group of 𝔻\mathbb{D}-automorphisms Aut𝔻⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{D}}(U) is the closed subgroup of Aut⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}(U) consisting of automorphisms preserving the set of decomposition groups {Uγ}γ∈ℒ^​(S)0\{U_{\gamma}\}_{{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0}}.

Remark 3.2.

In [7], Aut𝔻⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{D}}(U) was denoted by Aut∗⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}^{\ast}(U). According to [7, Proposition 7.2], the group Aut𝔻⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{D}}(U) preserve the set of all decomposition groups {Uσ}σ∈Cˇ​(S)\{U_{\sigma}\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)} of UU.

Let us introduce a slightly more restrictive condition, although in a more general context, which we will need later:

Definition 3.3.
  1. (i)

    For σ∈Cˇ​(S){\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S), we denote by I^σ{\hat{I}}_{\sigma} the closed abelian subgroup of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) topologically generated by the Dehn twists τγ\tau_{\gamma}, for γ∈σ{\gamma}\in{\sigma}. For HH a closed subgroup of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S), we then let I^σ​(H):=I^σ∩H{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}(H):={\hat{I}}_{\sigma}\cap H (the inertia group of HH associated to σ{\sigma}). The topological type of I^σ{\hat{I}}_{\sigma} is the topological type of σ{\sigma}.

  2. (ii)

    The group of 𝕀\mathbb{I}-automorphisms Aut𝕀⁡(H)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(H) is the closed subgroup of Aut⁡(H)\operatorname{Aut}(H) consisting of those elements which preserve the set of inertia groups {I^γ​(H)}γ∈ℒ^​(S)0\{{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}(H)\}_{{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0}}.

  3. (iii)

    We say that a subgroup KK of HH is 𝕀\mathbb{I}-characteristic if it is preserved by all elements of Aut𝕀⁡(H)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(H).

Remarks 3.4.

Let us observe that:

  1. (i)

    By [3, Proposition 6.8], for every open subgroup HH of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S), the assignment σ↦I^σ​(H){\sigma}\mapsto{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}(H) identifies the procongruence curve complex Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) with the simplicial profinite complex Cˇℐ⁡(H)​(S){\check{C}}_{{\mathcal{I}}(H)}(S) whose simplices are the inertia groups {Iσ​(H)}σ∈Cˇ​(S)\{I_{\sigma}(H)\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)}. In the sequel, we will identify all these complexes and denote them simply by Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S).

  2. (ii)

    For HH a closed subgroup of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S), we have Inn⁡H⊆Aut𝕀⁡(H)\operatorname{Inn}H\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(H). In particular, an 𝕀\mathbb{I}-characteristic subgroup of HH is normal.

Proposition 3.5.

We have:

  1. (i)

    An automorphism of HH is an 𝕀\mathbb{I}-automorphism if and only if it preserves the set of all inertia groups {I^σ​(H)}σ∈Cˇ​(S)\{{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}(H)\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)} of HH.

  2. (ii)

    For S≠S1,2S\neq S_{1,2} and HH any open subgroup of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S), the action of Aut𝕀⁡(H)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(H) on the set {I^σ​(H)}σ∈Cˇ​(S)\{{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}(H)\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)} preserves topological types.

  3. (iii)

    For H=Γ^​(S1,2)H={\widehat{\Gamma}}(S_{1,2}) or P​Γ^​(S1,2){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S_{1,2}), the action of Aut𝕀⁡(H)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(H) on the set {I^σ​(H)}σ∈Cˇ​(S)\{{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}(H)\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)} preserves topological types.

  4. (iv)

    Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) preserves the conjugacy classes of profinite braid twists in Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S).

Proof.

(i): One implication is obvious. For the other, let us observe that, for σ={γ0,…,γk}∈Cˇ​(S){\sigma}=\{{\gamma}_{0},\ldots,{\gamma}_{k}\}\in{\check{C}}(S), we have I^σ​(H)=∏i=0kI^γi​(H){\hat{I}}_{\sigma}(H)=\prod_{i=0}^{k}{\hat{I}}_{{\gamma}_{i}}(H). Moreover, by [7, Corollary 4.12], a set of nonperipheral profinite simple closed curves {γ0,…,γk}\{{\gamma}_{0},\ldots,{\gamma}_{k}\} forms a kk-simplex of Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) if and only if the associated profinite Dehn twists or, equivalently, some nontrivial powers of them commute. The conclusion is then clear.

(ii): Item (i) of Remarks 3.4 implies that, for every open subgroup HH of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S), there is a natural continuous homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(H)→Aut⁡(Cˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(H)\to\operatorname{Aut}({\check{C}}(S)). The conclusion then follows from [7, Theorem 5.5] (this is also where the hypothesis S≠S1,2S\neq S_{1,2} is actually needed).

(iii): Let us observe that an 𝕀\mathbb{I}-automorphism of Γ^​(S1,2){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S_{1,2}) preserves the subgroup P​Γ^​(S1,2){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S_{1,2}), since the latter is (topologically) generated by Dehn twists. Both statements then follow from [8, Lemma 2.19].

(iv): For n⁡(S)n(S) or k⁡(S)≥2k(S)\geq 2 (otherwise the claim is trivial), let bγ∈Γˇ​(S)b_{\gamma}\in{\check{\Gamma}}(S) be the profinite braid twist associated to a simple closed curve γ{\gamma} on SS bounding either a 22-punctured disc or a disc containing two boundary components.

By the previous item, for a given f∈Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))f\in\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)), we can assume, after composing with an element of Inn⁡Γˇ​(S)\operatorname{Inn}{\check{\Gamma}}(S), that ff preserves the inertia group I^γ=τγℤ^{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}=\tau_{\gamma}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}. In particular, ff preserves the normalizer NΓˇ​(S)​(I^γ)N_{{\check{\Gamma}}(S)}({\hat{I}}_{\gamma}) of I^γ{\hat{I}}_{\gamma} in Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S). From the description of this group (cf. [7, Corollary 4.12, (i)]), it follows that, for (g⁡(S),n⁡(S)+k⁡(S))≠(0,4),(1,2)(g(S),n(S)+k(S))\neq(0,4),(1,2), the center of NΓˇ​(S)​(I^γ)N_{{\check{\Gamma}}(S)}({\hat{I}}_{\gamma}) is generated by bγb_{\gamma}, which concludes the proof of item (ii) in this case.

For (g⁡(S),n⁡(S)+k⁡(S))=(0,4)(g(S),n(S)+k(S))=(0,4), a similar argument applies. For g⁡(S)=1g(S)=1 and either n⁡(S)=2n(S)=2 or k⁡(S)=2k(S)=2, the claim follows from (i) of Proposition 3.9. ∎

Remarks 3.6.

Let UU be an open subgroup of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S):

  1. (i)

    By [7, Corollary 4.12], we have that Inn⁡(U)⊆Aut𝕀⁡(U)⊆Aut𝔻⁡(U)\operatorname{Inn}(U)\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(U)\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{D}}(U). We denote by Out𝕀⁡(U)\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}(U) (resp. Out𝔻⁡(U)\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{D}}(U)) the group of outer 𝕀\mathbb{I}-automorphisms (resp. 𝔻\mathbb{D}-automorphisms) of UU.

  2. (ii)

    There is a natural faithful Galois representation ρℚ:Gℚ↪Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))\rho_{\mathbb{Q}}\colon\thinspace G_{\mathbb{Q}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)), where GℚG_{\mathbb{Q}} is the absolute Galois group of the rationals (cf. [3, Corollary 7.6]).

Except in the low genera cases, the 𝔻\mathbb{D}-condition and the 𝕀\mathbb{I}-condition are equivalent for full and pure procongruence mapping class groups. More precisely:

Proposition 3.7.

We have:

  1. (i)

    For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1 and S≠S1,2,S12,S2S\neq S_{1,2},S_{1}^{2},S_{2}, there holds:

    Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))=Out𝔻⁡(Γˇ​(S)).\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))=\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{D}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)).
  2. (ii)

    For S≠S1,1,S11,S2S\neq S_{1,1},S_{1}^{1},S_{2}, there holds:

    Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))=Out𝔻⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)).\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))=\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{D}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)).
  3. (iii)

    For S=S1,1,S11,S1,2,S12S=S_{1,1},S_{1}^{1},S_{1,2},S_{1}^{2} or S2S_{2}, there is a natural isomorphism:

    Out𝔻⁡(Γ^​(S))≅Out𝕀⁡(Γ^​(S))×{±1}.\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{D}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\times\{\pm 1\}.
Proof.

(i): for d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1 and S≠S1,2,S12,S2S\neq S_{1,2},S_{1}^{2},S_{2}, by [7, Corollary 4.12], we have Z⁡(Γˇ​(S)γ)=I^γZ({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma})={\hat{I}}_{\gamma} and NΓˇ​(S)​(I^γ)=Γˇ​(S)γN_{{\check{\Gamma}}(S)}({\hat{I}}_{\gamma})={\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma}, for all γ∈ℒ^​(S)0{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0}, and so the conclusion follows.

(ii): The same argument above applies to P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) in the given cases.

(iii): for S=S1,1,S11,S1,2,S12S=S_{1,1},S_{1}^{1},S_{1,2},S_{1}^{2} or S2S_{2}, by [7, Lemma 7.4], there is an exact sequence:

1→Hom⁡(Γ^​(S)/Z⁡(Γ^​(S)),Z⁡(Γ^​(S)))→Out⁡(Γ^​(S))→Out⁡(Γ^​(S)/Z⁡(Γ^​(S))),1\to\operatorname{Hom}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)),Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)))\to\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))),

where the center Z​(Γ^​(S))Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)) is generated by the hyperelliptic involution ι\iota and the abelianization of Γ^​(S)/Z​(Γ^​(S)){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)) is a cyclic group of finite even order (cf. [10, § 5.1.3]). Therefore we have Hom⁡(Γ^​(S)/Z⁡(Γ^​(S)),Z⁡(Γ^​(S)))≅{±1}\operatorname{Hom}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)),Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)))\cong\{\pm 1\}. Let us denote by ϕι\phi_{\iota} its generator.

By (i) and (ii), we have that Out𝔻⁡(Γ^​(S)/Z⁡(Γ^​(S)))=Out𝕀⁡(Γ^​(S)/Z⁡(Γ^​(S)))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{D}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)))=\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))).
