Since the intersection between the subgroups Out𝕀⁡(Γ^​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)) and Hom⁡(Γ^​(S)/Z⁡(Γ^​(S)),Z⁡(Γ^​(S)))\operatorname{Hom}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)),Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))) of Out⁡(Γ^​(S))\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)) is trivial and ϕι\phi_{\iota} normalizes Out𝕀⁡(Γ^​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)), the conclusion follows. ∎

3.2. The profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group

The inertia condition of the previous sections plays a central role in Grothendieck-Teichmüller theory. Let Aut♭⁡(Γ^0,n)\operatorname{Aut}^{\flat}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}) be the subgroup of of Aut⁡(Γ^0,n)\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}) consisting of those automorphisms which preserve the set of inertia groups {I^γ}γ∈ℒ^b​(S0,n)\{{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}\}_{{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}^{b}(S_{0,n})} and let Out♭⁡(Γ^0,n)\operatorname{Out}^{\flat}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}) be the corresponding outer automorphism group. The main theorem of Harbater and Schneps in [13] states that, for all n≥5n\geq 5, there is a natural isomorphism:

(3) Out♭⁡(Γ^0,n)≅Σn×GT^,\operatorname{Out}^{\flat}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n})\cong\Sigma_{n}\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}},

where GT^\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} is the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group introduced by Drinfeld (cf. [9]) and the symmetric group Σn\Sigma_{n} identifies with Inn⁡(Γ^0,[n])/Inn⁡(Γ^0,n)\operatorname{Inn}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]})/\operatorname{Inn}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}). The key case of this isomorphism is for n=5n=5 (cf. [13, Theorem 4]). This also allows to give a more intrinsic definition of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group letting (note that, for n=5n=5, the ♭\flat and 𝕀\mathbb{I}-conditions are equivalent):

GT^:=ZOut𝕀⁡(Γ^0,5)​(Σ5).\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}:=Z_{\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,5})}(\Sigma_{5}).

This characterization was further improved by Hoshi, Minamide and Mochizuki, who proved that Aut♭⁡(Γ^0,n)=Aut⁡(Γ^0,n)\operatorname{Aut}^{\flat}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n})=\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}) (cf. [16, Corollary 2.8]). Hence, for all n≥5n\geq 5, there is a natural isomorphism Out⁡(Γ^0,n)≅Σn×GT^\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n})\cong\Sigma_{n}\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} and, in particular, we have, even more intrinsically, that:

GT^=ZOut⁡(Γ^0,5)​(Σ5).\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}=Z_{\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,5})}(\Sigma_{5}).

Since Γ^0,n{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n} is a characteristic subgroup of Γ^0,[n]{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]} (cf. [24, Proposition 4.1, (ii)]), restriction of automorphisms induces a homomorphism Aut⁡(Γ^0,[n])→Aut⁡(Γ^0,n)\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]})\to\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}). We can then reformulate the above isomorphisms in the following way:

Proposition 3.8.

For n≥5n\geq 5, restriction of automorphisms induces an isomorphism Aut⁡(Γ^0,[n])≅Aut⁡(Γ^0,n)\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]})\cong\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}). In particular, for n≥5n\geq 5, there is a natural isomorphism:

(4) Out⁡(Γ^0,[n])≅GT^.\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]})\cong\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}.
Proof.

By [7, Theorem 4.14, (i)], for n≥5n\geq 5, the centralizer of Γ^0,n{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n} in Γ^0,[n]{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]} is trivial, so that the natural homomorphism Inn⁡(Γ^0,[n])→Aut⁡(Γ^0,n)\operatorname{Inn}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]})\to\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}) is injective. By [7, Lemma 3.3], the homomorphism Aut⁡(Γ^0,[n])→Aut⁡(Γ^0,n)\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]})\to\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}) is then also injective.

Let us consider the short exact sequence:

1→Γ^0,n→Γ^0,[n]→Σn→1.1\to{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}\to{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]}\to\Sigma_{n}\to 1.

In order to prove the proposition, we have to show that, for n≥5n\geq 5, every automorphism of Γ^0,n{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n} extends to Γ^0,[n]{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]}. For this, we will need [8, Lemma 2.18], which is based on Wells’ exact sequence (cf. [29, Theorem]).

Since the outer representation ρ:Σn→Out⁡(Γ^0,n)\rho\colon\thinspace\Sigma_{n}\to\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}) associated to the above short exact sequence is faithful and the center of Γ^0,n{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n} is trivial, the conditions of [8, Lemma 2.18, (i) and (iii)] are satisfied and we only need to check that condition (ii) is also satisfied. But this follows from the fact that ρ⁡(Σn)\rho(\Sigma_{n}) is a normal subgroup of Out⁡(Γ^0,n)\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n}), which is an immediate consequence of the fact that, as explained above, for n≥5n\geq 5, there is a natural isomorphism Out⁡(Γ^0,n)≅Σn×GT^\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n})\cong\Sigma_{n}\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}. ∎

The following result is essentially due to Minamide and Nakamura (cf. [24]):

Proposition 3.9.

For g⁡(S)=1g(S)=1 and, either n⁡(S)=2n(S)=2 and k⁡(S)=0k(S)=0, or n⁡(S)=0n(S)=0 and k⁡(S)=2k(S)=2, we have:

  1. (i)

    Out𝕀⁡(Γ^​(S))=Out𝕀⁡(P​Γ^​(S))=Out⁡(P​Γ^​(S))≅GT^\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))=\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))=\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}.

  2. (ii)

    Out⁡(Γ^​(S))≅{±1}×GT^\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\{\pm 1\}\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}.

Proof.

Since Γ⁡(S12)=Γ⁡(S1,2){\Gamma}(S_{1}^{2})={\Gamma}(S_{1,2}) and P​Γ​(S12)=P​Γ​(S1,2){\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S_{1}^{2})={\mathrm{P}\Gamma}(S_{1,2}), it is not restrictive to assume that k⁡(S)=0k(S)=0 and n⁡(S)=2n(S)=2. By [24, Corollary C], we know that Out⁡(P​Γ^​(S))≅GT^\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} which, in particular, implies that Out⁡(P​Γ^​(S))=Out𝕀⁡(P​Γ^​(S))\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))=\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)). It is then enough to prove that:

Out𝕀⁡(Γ^​(S))=Out𝕀⁡(P​Γ^​(S)) and Out⁡(Γ^​(S))≅{±1}×Out⁡(P​Γ^​(S)).\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))=\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\hskip 14.22636pt\mbox{ and }\hskip 14.22636pt\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\{\pm 1\}\times\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)).

The center Z​(Γ^​(S))Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)) is generated by the hyperelliptic involution ι\iota and Γ^​(S)=⟨ι⟩×P​Γ^​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)=\langle\iota\rangle\times{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) and so Γ^​(S)/Z⁡(Γ^​(S))≅P​Γ^​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\cong{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S). [7, Lemma 7.4] then implies that there is a split short exact sequence:

(5) 1→Hom(Γ^(S)/Z(Γ^(S))),Z(Γ^(S)))→Out(Γ^(S))→Out(PΓ^(S))→1.1\to\operatorname{Hom}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))),Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)))\to\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\to 1.

Since Hom⁡(Γ^​(S)/Z⁡(Γ^​(S)),Z⁡(Γ^​(S)))≅{±1}\operatorname{Hom}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)),Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)))\cong\{\pm 1\}, it follows Out⁡(Γ^​(S))≅{±1}×Out⁡(P​Γ^​(S))\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\{\pm 1\}\times\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)) as claimed above. By the description of the image of the group Hom⁡(Γ^​(S)/Z⁡(Γ^​(S)),Z⁡(Γ^​(S)))\operatorname{Hom}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)),Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))) in Out⁡(Γ^​(S))\operatorname{Out}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)), this has trivial intersection with Out𝕀⁡(Γ^​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)). The other claim above then also follows. ∎

3.3. Nonseparating inertia groups

Let C0​(S)C_{0}(S) be the nonseperating curve complex. It is the subcomplex of the curve complex C⁡(S)C(S) consisting of the simplices σ∈C⁡(S){\sigma}\in C(S) such that S∖σS\smallsetminus{\sigma} is connected. The procongruence nonseperating curve complex Cˇ0​(S){\check{C}}_{0}(S) is the abstract simplicial profinite complex whose set of kk-simplices is the closure of C0​(S)kC_{0}(S)_{k} in Cˇ​(S)k{\check{C}}(S)_{k}, for k≥0k\geq 0. In particular, a 00-simplex of Cˇ0​(S){\check{C}}_{0}(S) is determined by a profinite simple closed curve of nonseparating topological type. We denote by ℒ^ns​(S)\widehat{\mathcal{L}}^{\mathrm{ns}}(S) the closed subset of ℒ^​(S)\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S) consisting of such curves. The topological type of a simplex σ∈Cˇ0​(S){\sigma}\in{\check{C}}_{0}(S) is determined by its dimension. Note that, for g⁡(S)=0g(S)=0, we have C0​(S)=Cˇ0​(S)=∅C_{0}(S)={\check{C}}_{0}(S)=\emptyset.

Definition 3.10.

For HH a closed subgroup of the procongruence mapping class group Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S), the group of 𝕀0\mathbb{I}_{0}-automorphisms Aut𝕀0⁡(H)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(H) is the closed subgroup of Aut⁡(H)\operatorname{Aut}(H) consisting of those elements which preserve the set of inertia groups {I^γ​(H)}γ∈ℒ^ns​(S)\{{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}(H)\}_{{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}^{\mathrm{ns}}(S)}. We say that a subgroup KK of HH is 𝕀0\mathbb{I}_{0}-characteristic if it is preserved by all elements of Aut𝕀0⁡(H)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(H). Note that, for g⁡(S)=0g(S)=0, by definition, there holds Aut𝕀0⁡(H)=Aut⁡(H)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(H)=\operatorname{Aut}(H).

Remark 3.11.

Let us assume that HH is an open subgroup of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S). Then, the same argument of (i) of Proposition 3.5 shows that an element f∈Aut⁡(H)f\in\operatorname{Aut}(H) is an 𝕀0\mathbb{I}_{0}-automorphism if and only if ff preserves the set of inertia groups {Iσ​(H)}σ∈Cˇ0​(S)\{I_{\sigma}(H)\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}_{0}(S)} of HH. Moreover, from (ii) and (iii) of Proposition 3.5, it follows that, for either S≠S1,2S\neq S_{1,2} or H=Γˇ​(S1,2),P​Γˇ​(S1,2)H={\check{\Gamma}}(S_{1,2}),{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S_{1,2}), there holds Aut𝕀⁡(H)≤Aut𝕀0⁡(H)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(H)\leq\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(H).

In fact, for pure procongruence mapping class groups, the 𝕀\mathbb{I}-condition turns out to be no more restrictive than the 𝕀0\mathbb{I}_{0}-condition:

Theorem 3.12.

For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, we have Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))=Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))=\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)).

Proof.

We proceed by induction on the genus of SS. The base for the induction will be provided by the cases g⁡(S)=0,1g(S)=0,1, which we will treat separately in the following lemmas.

For g⁡(S)=0g(S)=0, we have the following result which improves [16, Corollary 2.8]:

Lemma 3.13.

For n≥5n\geq 5, we have Aut𝕀⁡(Γ^0,n)=Aut⁡(Γ^0,n)≅Aut⁡(Γ^0,[n])=Aut𝕀⁡(Γ^0,[n])\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n})=\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n})\cong\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]})=\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]}).

Proof.

The first identity is [8, Theorem 6.6] while the isomorphism in the middle follows from Proposition 3.8. The third identity then also follows. ∎

Lemma 3.14.

For n≥2n\geq 2, we have Aut𝕀⁡(Γ^1,n)=Aut𝕀0⁡(Γ^1,n)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,n})=\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,n}).

Proof.

The case n=2n=2 follows from (ii) of Proposition 3.9 and the observation that, in the short exact sequence (cf. [7, Lemma 7.4]):

1→Hom⁡(Γ^1,2/Z⁡(Γ^1,2),Z⁡(Γ^1,2))→Aut⁡(Γ^1,2)→Aut⁡(Γ^1,2/Z⁡(Γ^1,2)),1\to\operatorname{Hom}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,2}/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,2}),Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,2}))\to\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,2})\to\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,2}/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,2})),

the image of Hom⁡(Γ^1,2/Z⁡(Γ^1,2),Z⁡(Γ^1,2))\operatorname{Hom}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,2}/Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,2}),Z({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,2})) has trivial intersection with Aut𝕀0⁡(Γ^1,2)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,2}).

For n≥3n\geq 3, it is enough to prove that, for any f∈Aut𝕀0⁡(Γ^1,n)f\in\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,n}) and γ∈ℒ​(S)0⊂ℒ^​(S)0{\gamma}\in{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0}\subset\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0} separating, we have f⁡(I^γ)=I^γ′f({\hat{I}}_{\gamma})={\hat{I}}_{{\gamma}^{\prime}}, for some γ′∈ℒ^​(S)0{\gamma}^{\prime}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0}. Let α\alpha be a nonseparating simple closed curve on SS such that τγ∈Γα\tau_{\gamma}\in{\Gamma}_{\alpha}. After composing ff with a suitable inner automorphism, we can assume that ff preserves the stabilizer Γ^α{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{\alpha}. According to (ii) of Theorem 2.3, this group is described by the short exact sequence:

1→I^α→Γ^α→Γ^0,n+2→1.1\to{\hat{I}}_{\alpha}\to{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{\alpha}\to{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n+2}\to 1.

Therefore, ff induces an automorphism f¯\bar{f} of the quotient group Γ^α/I^α≅Γ^0,n+2{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{\alpha}/{\hat{I}}_{\alpha}\cong{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n+2}. Let us denote by I¯γ\bar{I}_{\gamma} the image of I^γ{\hat{I}}_{\gamma} in this quotient. By Lemma 3.13, we have that f¯​(I¯γ)=I^γ¯′\bar{f}(\bar{I}_{\gamma})={\hat{I}}_{\bar{\gamma}^{\prime}}, for some profinite simple closed curve γ¯′\bar{\gamma}^{\prime} on S0,n+2S_{0,n+2}.

Let γ′∈ℒ^​(S1,n){\gamma}^{\prime}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S_{1,n}) be a lift of γ¯′\bar{\gamma}^{\prime}. Then, γ′{\gamma}^{\prime} is also of separating type and there is an identity f⁡(τγ)=τγ′h​ταkf(\tau_{\gamma})=\tau_{{\gamma}^{\prime}}^{h}\tau_{\alpha}^{k}, for some h∈ℤ^∗h\in{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}^{\ast} and k∈ℤ^k\in{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}. The kernel of the natural epimorphism Γ^1,n→Γ^1,1{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,n}\to{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,1} is topologically generated by elements of the form τβ1h​τβ2−h\tau_{\beta_{1}}^{h}\tau_{\beta_{2}}^{-h}, with β1,β2∈ℒ^ns​(S)\beta_{1},\beta_{2}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}^{\mathrm{ns}}(S) and h∈ℤ^∗h\in{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}^{\ast}, and is therefore preserved by ff. In particular, f⁡(τγ)f(\tau_{\gamma}) belongs to this kernel. By projecting the identity f⁡(τγ)=τγ′h​ταkf(\tau_{\gamma})=\tau_{{\gamma}^{\prime}}^{h}\tau_{\alpha}^{k} to Γ^1,1{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{1,1}, we then see that k=0k=0, which concludes the proof of the lemma. ∎

We now proceed to the proof of Theorem 3.12 by induction on the genus. The base for the induction is provided by Lemma 3.14. So let us assume that the statement of Theorem 3.12 holds in genus g−1≥1g-1\geq 1 and let us prove it for genus g=g⁡(S)g=g(S). For simplicity, let us denote by {I^σ}σ∈Cˇ​(S)\{{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)} the set of inertia groups of P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S). The key observation is that the hypothesis g⁡(S)≥2g(S)\geq 2 implies that a kk-simplex σ∈C⁡(S){\sigma}\in C(S), for k=d⁡(S)−1,d⁡(S)−2k=d(S)-1,d(S)-2, contains at least a nonseparating curve.

From the induction hypothesis, we will deduce that Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) preserves the subsets of inertia groups {I^σ}σ∈Cˇ​(S)k\{{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)_{k}}, for k=d⁡(S)−1,d⁡(S)−2k=d(S)-1,d(S)-2. In fact, if α∈σ\alpha\in{\sigma} is nonseparating, after composing a given f∈Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))f\in\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) with an inner automorphism, we can assume that f⁡(α)=αf(\alpha)=\alpha, so that ff restricts to an automorphism of the stabilizer P​Γˇ​(S)α{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\alpha} which preserves the inertia group I^α{\hat{I}}_{\alpha} and is contained in Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)α)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\alpha}). Since I^σ⊂P​Γˇ​(S)α{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}\subset{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\alpha} and P​Γˇ​(S)α/I^α≅P​Γˇ​(S∖α){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\alpha}/{\hat{I}}_{\alpha}\cong{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus\alpha), the induction hypothesis implies that the automorphism f¯\bar{f} induced by ff on the quotient P​Γˇ​(S)α/I^α{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\alpha}/{\hat{I}}_{\alpha} has the property that f¯​(I^σ/I^α)=I^σ′/I^α\bar{f}({\hat{I}}_{\sigma}/{\hat{I}}_{\alpha})={\hat{I}}_{{\sigma}^{\prime}}/{\hat{I}}_{\alpha}, for some α∈σ′∈Cˇ​(S)k\alpha\in{\sigma}^{\prime}\in{\check{C}}(S)_{k}, for k=d⁡(S)−1,d⁡(S)−2k=d(S)-1,d(S)-2, and then f⁡(I^σ)=I^σ′f({\hat{I}}_{\sigma})={\hat{I}}_{{\sigma}^{\prime}}.

We can now proceed as in the proof of [8, Theorem 6.6]. Let us identify (cf. (i) of Remarks 3.4) the procongruence curve complex Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) with the abstract simplicial profinite complex whose set of kk-simplices is the set of closed subgroups {I^σ}σ∈Cˇk​(S)\{{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}_{k}(S)}. The dual graph Cˇ∗​(S){\check{C}}^{\ast}(S) of Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) (cf. [7, Definition 3.9]) has then for vertex set the set {I^σ}σ∈Cˇ​(S)d⁡(S)−1\{{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)_{d(S)-1}} and two such vertices I^σ{\hat{I}}_{\sigma} and I^σ′{\hat{I}}_{{\sigma}^{\prime}} are connected by an edge if and only if |σ∩σ′|=d⁡(S)−1|{\sigma}\cap{\sigma}^{\prime}|=d(S)-1. This happens if and only if I^σ∩I^σ′{\hat{I}}_{\sigma}\cap{\hat{I}}_{{\sigma}^{\prime}} equals I^σ∩σ′{\hat{I}}_{{\sigma}\cap{\sigma}^{\prime}} and is a free ℤ^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}-module of rank d⁡(S)−1d(S)-1.

The remarks above then imply that the natural action of Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) on the set of closed subgroups of P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) induces a representation Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Aut⁡(Cˇ∗​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Aut}({\check{C}}^{\ast}(S)).

By [7, Lemma 6.5], the procongruence curve complex Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) can be reconstructed from its dual graph Cˇ∗​(S){\check{C}}^{\ast}(S) and there is a natural isomorphism Aut⁡(Cˇ∗​(S))≅Aut⁡(Cˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}({\check{C}}^{\ast}(S))\cong\operatorname{Aut}({\check{C}}(S)). It then follows that the action of Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) on the set of closed subgroups preserves the set of all inertia groups of P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S). ∎

For g⁡(S)≥1g(S)\geq 1, the pure procongruence mapping class group P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) is topologically generated by nonseparating Dehn twists. It is then an 𝕀0\mathbb{I}_{0}-characteristic subgroup of the full procongruence mapping class group Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S). We already observed that, by [24, Proposition 4.1, (ii)], Γ^0,n{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,n} is a characteristic subgroup of Γ^0,[n]{\widehat{\Gamma}}_{0,[n]}. Therefore, restriction of 𝕀0\mathbb{I}_{0}-automorphisms from Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) to P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) defines a natural homomorphism Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)). Since Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))≤Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\leq\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) (cf. Remark 3.11), from Theorem 3.12, it follows:

Corollary 3.15.

For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, we have Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))=Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))=\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)).

4. Extending 𝕀\mathbb{I}-automorphisms

The main result of this section is the following:

Theorem 4.1.

Let S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} be a hyperbolic surface with d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1. Let us recall the notation S̊:=S∖∂S\ring{S}:=S\smallsetminus{\partial S}. We then have:

  1. (i)

    Restriction of automorphisms induces an isomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S̊))≅Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S}))\cong\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)).

  2. (ii)

    For (g,n+k)≠(1,2)(g,n+k)\neq(1,2), there is a natural isomorphism:

    Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))≅Σn+k×Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S̊)).\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\Sigma_{n+k}\times\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S})).
  3. (iii)

    For (g,n+k)=(1,2)(g,n+k)=(1,2), there holds Out𝕀⁡(P​Γ^​(S))=Out𝕀⁡(Γ^​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))=\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)).

4.1. Preliminary lemmas

Thanks to the results of [8], there is a useful criterion to determine whether an 𝕀\mathbb{I}-automorphism of P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) is induced by an inner automorphism of Γˇ​(S̊){\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S}). After identifying the procongruence curve complex Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) with the simplicial profinite complex whose simplices are the inertia groups {Iσ}σ∈Cˇ​(S)\{I_{\sigma}\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)} (cf. (i) of Remarks 3.4), the vertices of the procongruence pants complex CˇP​(S){\check{C}}_{P}(S) are identified with the set {Iσ}σ∈Cˇ​(S)d⁡(S)−1\{I_{\sigma}\}_{{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)_{d(S)-1}} of inertia subgroups of maximal rank. We then have:

Lemma 4.2.

Let ϕ∈Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\phi\in\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) be an element which, via the natural representation Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Aut⁡(Cˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Aut}({\check{C}}(S)), acts trivially on the simplices corresponding to the vertices of a profinite Farey subgraph F^μ{\widehat{\operatorname{F}}}_{\mu} of CˇP​(S){\check{C}}_{P}(S) (cf. [7, Definition 6.3]). Then, ϕ∈Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S̊))\phi\in\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S})).

Proof.

It is not restrictive to assume ∂S=∅\partial S=\emptyset. For d⁡(S)=1d(S)=1 the claim is trivial. For d⁡(S)≥2d(S)\geq 2, [8, Theorem 2.17] implies that ϕ∈Inn⁡(Γˇ±​(S̊))\phi\in\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}^{\pm}(\ring{S})), where Γˇ±​(S̊){\check{\Gamma}}^{\pm}(\ring{S}) is the congruence completion of the extended mapping class group Γ±​(S̊){\Gamma}^{\pm}(\ring{S}). Since, by hypothesis, in particular, ϕ\phi preserves the orientation of the profinite Farey subgraph F^μ{\widehat{\operatorname{F}}}_{\mu}, from [8, Theorem 2.2], it follows that ϕ∈Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S̊))\phi\in\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S})). ∎

Let us also observe that:

Lemma 4.3.

Let S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} and assume that (g,n+k)≠(0,4)(g,n+k)\neq(0,4). Then, the natural homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) is injective.

Proof.

The claim is trivial for n⁡(S)≤1n(S)\leq 1, while, for g⁡(S)=1g(S)=1 and n⁡(S)=2n(S)=2, k⁡(S)=0k(S)=0, or n⁡(S)=0n(S)=0, k⁡(S)=2k(S)=2, it follows from (i) of Proposition 3.9. Since (g,n+k)≠(0,4)(g,n+k)\neq(0,4), by [7, Theorem 4.14], we can then assume that the centralizer of P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) in Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) is trivial, so that the natural homomorphism Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) is injective. By [7, Lemma 3.3], the homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) is then also injective. ∎

The following lemma will be essential for the proof of Theorem 4.1:

Lemma 4.4.

For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, the natural monomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S̊))↪Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S}))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) identifies Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S̊))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S})) with a normal subgroup of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)).

Proof.

Since P​Γˇ​(S)=P​Γˇ​(S̊){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)={\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S}), it is not restrictive to assume that ∂S=∅\partial S=\emptyset and so S̊=S\ring{S}=S. Let us also observe that Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) is generated by its normal subgroup P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) and braid twists.

Since Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) is a normal subgroup of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)), it is then enough to show that, for a given braid twist bγb_{\gamma}, where γ∈ℒb​(S){\gamma}\in{\mathcal{L}}^{b}(S), for every f∈Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))f\in\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)), we have that ϕ:=f∘inn⁡bγ∘f−1∈Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))\phi:=f\circ\operatorname{inn}b_{\gamma}\circ f^{-1}\in\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)). The key observation is that, since inn⁡bγ\operatorname{inn}b_{\gamma} restricts to the identity on the stabilizer P​Γˇ​(S)γ{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma}, the automorphism ϕ\phi restricts to the identity on the stabilizer P​Γˇ​(S)f⁡(γ){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{f({\gamma})}. Since, for every σ∈Cˇ​(S)d⁡(S)−2{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)_{d(S)-2} such that γ∈σ{\gamma}\in{\sigma}, the vertices of the profinite Farey subgraph F^f⁡(σ)⊂CˇP​(S){\widehat{\operatorname{F}}}_{f({\sigma})}\subset{\check{C}}_{P}(S) are subgroups of the stabilizer P​Γˇ​(S)f⁡(γ){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{f({\gamma})}, the action of ϕ\phi restricts to the identity on the vertices of all these profinite Farey subgraphs. By Lemma 4.2, we then conclude that ϕ∈Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))\phi\in\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)). ∎

Note that for S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} and (g,n+k)≠(1,2)(g,n+k)\neq(1,2), the quotient Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S̊))/Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\left.\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S}))\right/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) identifies with the quotient Γˇ​(S̊)/P​Γˇ​(S)≅Σn+k{\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S})/{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)\cong\Sigma_{n+k}. From Lemma 4.4, it then follows that Σn+k\Sigma_{n+k} identifies with a normal subgroup of Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)). We have:

Lemma 4.5.

For S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} a hyperbolic surface such that (g,n+k)≠(1,2)(g,n+k)\neq(1,2), restriction of inner automorphisms induces an epimorphism Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Inn⁡Σn+k\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Inn}\Sigma_{n+k}.

Proof.

We can assume that n+k≥2n+k\geq 2 and, since (g,n+k)≠(1,2)(g,n+k)\neq(1,2), in particular, that the center of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) is trivial. By the results of [27], it is enough to show that an automorphism of Σn+k\Sigma_{n+k} induced by restriction of an element of Inn⁡(Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)))\operatorname{Inn}(\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))) sends a transposition to another transposition. This follows from the fact that, by (iv) of Proposition 3.5, the conjugacy action of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) on its normal subgroup Inn⁡Γˇ​(S)≅Γˇ​(S)\operatorname{Inn}{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\cong{\check{\Gamma}}(S) sends a profinite braid twist to another profinite braid twists, since it preserves conjugacy classes of profinite Dehn twists. ∎

In particular, for n+k>2n+k>2, there is a natural epimorphism Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Σn+k\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\Sigma_{n+k} which is a left inverse of the inclusion Σn+k↪Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\Sigma_{n+k}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)). For g>1g>1, this is also true for n+k=2n+k=2, thanks to the following lemma:

Lemma 4.6.

For S=Sg,nS=S_{g,n} such that either g≥1g\geq 1 and (g,n)≠(1,2)(g,n)\neq(1,2) or g=0g=0 and n≥5n\geq 5, there is an epimorphism Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Σn\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\Sigma_{n}, such that its composition with the homomorphism inn:Γˇ​(S)→Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{inn}\colon\thinspace{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) is the natural epimorphism Γˇ​(S)→Σn{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\to\Sigma_{n}.

Proof.

The statement of the lemma is similar to [8, Lemma 4.2] and is proved essentially in the same way. ∎

4.2. Proof of Theorem 4.1

We can assume n+k≥2n+k\geq 2, otherwise the theorem is trivial. For the proof of item (i) and (ii) of the theorem, it is not restrictive to assume ∂S=∅{\partial S}=\emptyset.

(i): For S=S1,2S=S_{1,2}, this is just (i) of Proposition 3.9. Therefore, we can also assume S≠S1,2S\neq S_{1,2} and then, by [7, Theorem 4.14, (i)], that the centralizer of P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) in Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) is trivial.

We have to show that the natural monomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))↪Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) (cf. Lemma 4.3) is surjective. For this, as in the proof of Proposition 3.8, we consider the short exact sequence:

1→P​Γˇ​(S)→Γˇ​(S)→Σn→1.1\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\to\Sigma_{n}\to 1.

Let ρ:Σn→Out⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\rho\colon\thinspace\Sigma_{n}\to\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) be the outer representation associated to the above short exact sequence. The image of Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) in Out⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) coincides with ρ⁡(Σn)\rho(\Sigma_{n}). From Lemma 4.4, it then follows that ρ⁡(Σn)\rho(\Sigma_{n}) is a normal subgroup of Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)).

Since ZΓˇ​(S)​(P​Γˇ​(S))={1}Z_{{\check{\Gamma}}(S)}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))=\{1\}, we have that Σn≅Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))/Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))⊂Out⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\Sigma_{n}\cong\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\left/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\right.\subset\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)), so that the representation ρ\rho is faithful. The same argument of the proof of Proposition 3.8 then implies that every automorphism f∈Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))f\in\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) extends to Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S), thus completing the proof of the first item.

(ii): By the previous item of the theorem, there is a short exact sequence:

1→Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))/Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))/Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))/Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))→1.1\to\left.\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\right/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\left.\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\right/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\left.\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\right/\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to 1.

Since, by hypothesis, n≠2n\neq 2 for g=1g=1, there holds Z⁡(Γˇ​(S))=Z⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))={1}Z({\check{\Gamma}}(S))=Z({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))=\{1\} and so we have Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))/Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))≅Γˇ​(S)/P​Γˇ​(S)≅Σn\left.\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\right/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\left.{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\right/{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)\cong\Sigma_{n}. By Lemma 4.6, the monomorphism Σn↪Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\Sigma_{n}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) has a left inverse Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Σn\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\Sigma_{n} which provides the splitting.

(iii): For S=S1,11S=S_{1,1}^{1}, we have P​Γ^​(S)≅Γ^​(S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)\cong{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) and the statement is trivial. For S=S1,2S=S_{1,2} or S12S_{1}^{2}, this is just the first item of Proposition 3.9.

4.3. Inertia conditions for procongruence relative mapping class groups

For a surface S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} with boundary ∂S=∪i=1kδi{\partial S}=\cup_{i=1}^{k}\delta_{i}, let S~≅Sg,n+2​k{\widetilde{S}}\cong S_{g,n+2k} be the surface introduced in Definition 2.5. The natural embedding S↪S~S\hookrightarrow{\widetilde{S}} induces a monomorphism of procongruence mapping class groups Γˇ​(S,∂S)↪Γˇ​(S~){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\hookrightarrow{\check{\Gamma}}({\widetilde{S}}) (cf. Section 2.7). Therefore, Definition 3.3 also applies to procongruence relative mapping class groups. Note that ∏i=1kτδiℤ^\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} is the maximal normal inertia subgroup of Γˇ​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}). We call it the normal inertia group of Γˇ​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}). From (iii) of Proposition 2.6, it follows that this subgroup is also 𝕀\mathbb{I}-characteristic. In particular, there is a natural homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))→Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)).

Definition 4.7.

As we observed above, by Definition 3.3, for an open subgroup UU of Γˇ​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}), the group Aut𝕀⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(U) is defined to be the subgroup of Aut⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}(U) consisting of those automorphisms which preserve the inertia groups {I^γ​(U)}γ∈ℒ^​(S~)0\{{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}(U)\}_{{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}({\widetilde{S}})_{0}}. We then let Aut𝕀0⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(U) to be the subgroup of Aut⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}(U) consisting of those automorphisms which preserve the set of inertia groups {I^γ​(U)}γ∈ℒ^ns​(S)∪{I^δi​(U)}i=1,…,k\{{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}(U)\}_{{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}^{\mathrm{ns}}(S)}\cup\{{\hat{I}}_{\delta_{i}}(U)\}_{i=1,\dots,k} (note that ℒ^ns​(S)≡ℒ^ns​(S~)\widehat{\mathcal{L}}^{\mathrm{ns}}(S)\equiv\widehat{\mathcal{L}}^{\mathrm{ns}}({\widetilde{S}})).

From (iii) of Proposition 2.6, it follows that the normal inertia group A:=U∩∏i=1kτδiℤ^A:=U\cap\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} of UU is an 𝕀\mathbb{I}-characteristic subgroup of UU. From Definition 4.7, it then follows that it is also 𝕀0\mathbb{I}_{0}-characteristic in UU. In particular, if we let U¯:=U/A\overline{U}:=U/A, there are natural homomorphisms Aut𝕀⁡(U)→Aut𝕀⁡(U¯)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(U)\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(\overline{U}) and Aut𝕀0⁡(U)→Aut𝕀0⁡(U¯)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(U)\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(\overline{U}).

We say that a group GG is virtually (topologically) generated by a subset TT, if GG contains a finite index subgroup (topologically) generated by this subset.

Lemma 4.8.

We have:

  1. (i)

    Let UU be an open subgroup of Γˇ​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) virtually topologically generated by the inertia groups {I^γ​(U)}γ∈ℒ^​(S~)0\{{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}(U)\}_{{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}({\widetilde{S}})_{0}}. Then, the natural homomorphisms:

    Aut𝕀⁡(U)→Aut𝕀⁡(U¯)×Aut⁡(A) and Out𝕀⁡(U)→Out𝕀⁡(U¯)×Aut⁡(A)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(U)\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(\overline{U})\times\operatorname{Aut}(A)\hskip 11.38092pt\mbox{ and }\hskip 11.38092pt\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}(U)\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}(\overline{U})\times\operatorname{Aut}(A)

    are injective.

  2. (ii)

    Let UU be an open subgroup of Γˇ​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) virtually topologically generated by the inertia groups {I^γ​(U)}γ∈ℒ^ns​(S)∪{I^δi​(U)}i=1,…,k\{{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}(U)\}_{{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}^{\mathrm{ns}}(S)}\cup\{{\hat{I}}_{\delta_{i}}(U)\}_{i=1,\dots,k}. Then, the natural homomorphisms:

    Aut𝕀0⁡(U)→Aut𝕀0⁡(U¯)×Aut⁡(A) and Out𝕀0⁡(U)→Out𝕀0⁡(U¯)×Aut⁡(A)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(U)\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(\overline{U})\times\operatorname{Aut}(A)\hskip 11.38092pt\mbox{ and }\hskip 11.38092pt\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(U)\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(\overline{U})\times\operatorname{Aut}(A)

    are injective.

Proof.

It is enough to prove the first item since the proof of the second is basically the same. By [7, Lemma 7.4], the kernel of the homomorphism Aut⁡(U)A→Aut⁡(U¯)×Aut⁡(A)\operatorname{Aut}(U)_{A}\to\operatorname{Aut}(\overline{U})\times\operatorname{Aut}(A) (resp. Out⁡(U)A→Out⁡(U¯)×Aut⁡(A)\operatorname{Out}(U)_{A}\to\operatorname{Out}(\overline{U})\times\operatorname{Aut}(A)) identifies with the (free) abelian group Hom⁡(U¯,A)\operatorname{Hom}(\overline{U},A).

The restriction of a homomorphism ϕ∈Hom⁡(U¯,A)∩Aut𝕀⁡(U)\phi\in\operatorname{Hom}(\overline{U},A)\cap\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(U) to the finite index subgroup of U¯\overline{U} topologically generated by inertia groups is trivial. Since AA is torsion free, this implies that ϕ\phi itself is trivial and hence that Hom⁡(U¯,A)∩Aut𝕀⁡(U)={1}\operatorname{Hom}(\overline{U},A)\cap\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(U)=\{1\}. ∎

Let us observe that P​Γˇ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}), for g⁡(S)≥1g(S)\geq 1, is topologically generated by nonseparating Dehn twists, so that Γˇ​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) is virtually topologically generated by them. An immediate consequence of Lemma 4.8 and Theorem 3.12 is then:

Proposition 4.9.

For g⁡(S)≥1g(S)\geq 1, there holds Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))=Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))=\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) and Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))=Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))=\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})).

4.4. Extending automorphisms of procongruence relative mapping class groups

In this section, we will prove a version of Theorem 4.1 for procongruence relative mapping class groups. For this, we will need a series of preliminary lemmas.

The subgroup P​Γˇ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) of Γˇ​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) is 𝕀\mathbb{I}-characteristic. There is then a natural homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))→Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) and, from Lemma 4.3 and (i) of Lemma 4.8, it follows:

Lemma 4.10.

Let S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} and assume that (g,n+k)≠(0,4)(g,n+k)\neq(0,4). Then, the natural homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))→Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) is injective.

For (g,n+k)≠(0,4)(g,n+k)\neq(0,4), let us identify Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) with a subgroup of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) by means of the above monomorphism. We then have:

Lemma 4.11.

For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, there holds Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))⊲Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\lhd\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})).

Proof.

Composing the natural monomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))↪Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) (cf. Lemma 4.10) with the monomorphism of (ii), Lemma 4.8, we can identify Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) with a subgroup of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))×Aut⁡(∏i=1kτδiℤ^)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\times\operatorname{Aut}(\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}). Let us then observe that, for S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k}, the image of Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) in the quotient Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))×Aut⁡(∏i=1kτδiℤ^)\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\times\operatorname{Aut}(\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}) identifies with:

Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))/Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))≅Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))/Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))≅Σn×Σk.\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\left/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\right.\cong\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\left/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\right.\cong\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}.

From Lemma 4.4 (and its proof), it then follows that the image of the group Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) inside Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))×Aut⁡(∏i=1kτδiℤ^)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\times\operatorname{Aut}(\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}) is normalized by the image of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})). ∎

We also have:

Lemma 4.12.

For S=Sg,nk≠S1,2S=S_{g,n}^{k}\neq S_{1,2} a hyperbolic surface, there is a natural epimorphism Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))→Σn×Σk\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\to\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}, such that its composition with the homomorphism inn:Γˇ​(S,∂S)→Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{inn}\colon\thinspace{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) is the natural epimorphism Γˇ​(S,∂S)→Σn×Σk{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}.

Proof.

For n=0n=0 and k>0k>0, we consider the action of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) on the normal inertia subgroup ∏i=1kτδiℤ^\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} induced by restriction of inner automorphisms. This action permutes the procyclic subgroups τδiℤ^\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} and defines an epimorphism Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))→Σk\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\to\Sigma_{k} with the desired properties.

For n>0n>0, we consider the natural homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))→Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)). We then get, for g=0g=0, by the isomorphism (3), and, for g>0g>0, (g,n+k)≠(1,2)(g,n+k)\neq(1,2), by Lemma 4.6, a homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))→Σn+k\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\to\Sigma_{n+k} compatible with the natural homomorphisms Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))↪Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) and Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))↠Σn×Σk⊆Σn+k\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\twoheadrightarrow\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}\subseteq\Sigma_{n+k}.

Let {γ0,γ1}∈C⁡(S)⊂Cˇ​(S)\{{\gamma}_{0},{\gamma}_{1}\}\in C(S)\subset{\check{C}}(S) be a 11-simplex bounding an annulus in SS containing a boundary component of the surface. From the description of the normalizer in P​Γˇ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) of the closed subgroup topologically generated by τγ0\tau_{{\gamma}_{0}} and τγ1\tau_{{\gamma}_{1}} (cf. Theorem 2.8), it easily follows that an element of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) maps the simplex {γ0,γ1}\{{\gamma}_{0},{\gamma}_{1}\} to another simplex of Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) which has the same topological type, that is to say which is in the Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S)-orbit of a 11-simplex in C⁡(S)C(S) consisting of curves which also bound an annulus in SS.

Therefore, the action of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) on the set of all punctures and boundary components of S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} preserves the partition of this set into punctures and boundary components. This means that the image of the homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))→Σn+k\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\to\Sigma_{n+k} defined above is the subgroup Σn×Σk\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}, which stabilizes this partition. The second claim of the lemma is also clear. ∎

The analogue of Theorem 4.1 then holds:

Theorem 4.13.

Let S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} be a hyperbolic surface such that d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1.

  1. (i)

    Restriction of automorphisms induces an isomorphism:

    Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))≅Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)).\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\cong\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})).
  2. (ii)

    For S≠S1,2S\neq S_{1,2}, there is a natural isomorphism:

    Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))≅Σn×Σk×Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S)).\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\cong\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}\times\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})).
Proof.

(i): We can assume k>0k>0 and then, since d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, that the centers of P​Γˇ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) and Γˇ​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) do not contain a hyperelliptic involution. We have to show that the natural monomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))↪Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) (cf. Lemma 4.10) is surjective. For this, we consider the short exact sequence:

1→P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)→Γˇ​(S,∂S)→Σn×Σk→1.1\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}\to 1.

By Lemma 4.11 and item (iii) of Proposition 2.6, we can then argue as in the proof of the first item of Theorem 4.1.

(ii): By the first item of Theorem 4.13, proved above, and Lemma 4.12, we can argue as in the proof of item (ii) of Theorem 4.1. ∎

5. Homomorphisms between outer automorphism groups of procongruence mapping class groups

In this section, we will assume that SS is a hyperbolic surface with empty boundary.

5.1. Functorial homomorphisms

Let γ{\gamma} be a nonseparating simple closed curve on SS. By (ii) of Theorem 2.3, there is a short exact sequence:

1→τγℤ^→P​Γˇ​(S)γ→→P​Γˇ​(S∖γ)→1.1\to\tau_{\gamma}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})\to 1.

Since the group P​Γˇ​(S∖γ){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}) is center free (cf. [3, Corollary 6.2]), we have Z⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)=τγℤ^Z({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})=\tau_{\gamma}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}.

We want to construct a natural homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})). The first step is to construct a homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}).

Remark 5.1.

Note that, for UU an open subgroup of Γˇ​(S)γ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma} (e.g. P​Γˇ​(S)γ→{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}), the nontrivial inertia groups of UU are parameterized by the subcomplex Star​(γ)⊂Cˇ​(S)\mathrm{Star}({\gamma})\subset{\check{C}}(S) while the nontrivial inertia groups of the image of UU via the natural homomorphism Γˇ​(S)γ→Γˇ​(S∖γ){\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma}\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}) are parameterized by the subcomplex Link⁡(γ)≅Cˇ​(S∖γ)⊂Cˇ​(S)\operatorname{Link}({\gamma})\cong{\check{C}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})\subset{\check{C}}(S) (cf. [3, Remark 4.7]).

We then proceed as in the proof of [3, Theorem 7.4]. Let us choose an orientation for every element of ℒ^​(S)\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S) (cf. [3, Section 4]). By definition, an element f∈Γˇ​(S)γf\in{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma} preserves the orientation chosen for γ{\gamma} if and only if f∈Γˇ​(S)γ→f\in{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}.

For f∈Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))f\in\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)), by items (ii) and (iii) of Proposition 3.5, there is an element x∈P​Γˇ​(S)x\in{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) such that inn⁡x∘f\operatorname{inn}x\circ f preserves the inertia group IγI_{\gamma} and, by [7, Corollary 4.12, (i)], also the decomposition group P​Γˇ​(S)γ{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma}. Let us then observe that P​Γˇ​(S)γ→{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}} is a 𝕀\mathbb{I}-characteristic subgroup of P​Γˇ​(S)γ{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma}, because it is (topologically) generated by the profinite Dehn twists contained in P​Γˇ​(S)γ{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma}. Hence, by restriction, inn⁡x∘f\operatorname{inn}x\circ f induces an automorphism of P​Γˇ​(S)γ→{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}.

Since there is an element of P​Γˇ​(S)γ{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma} which reverses the orientation of γ{\gamma}, we can choose the element x∈P​Γˇ​(S)x\in{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) in a way that it sends the orientation fixed on γ{\gamma} to the orientation fixed on x⁡(γ)x({\gamma}). If y∈P​Γˇ​(S)y\in{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) is another such element, then x​y−1∈P​Γˇ​(S)γ→xy^{-1}\in{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}. In this way, the automorphism inn⁡x∘f\operatorname{inn}x\circ f is determined by ff modulo an inner automorphism of P​Γˇ​(S)γ→{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}, so that we get a natural homomorphism:

(6) P​R~γ:Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→).\tilde{PR}_{\gamma}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}).

Since Z⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)=τγℤ^Z({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})=\tau_{\gamma}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} is a characteristic subgroup of P​Γˇ​(S)γ→{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}, there is also a natural homomorphism Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)→Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→/τγℤ^)≅Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}(\left.{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}\right/\tau_{\gamma}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}})\cong\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})). Composing with the homomorphism (6), we get the natural homomorphism:

P​Rγ:Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ)).PR_{\gamma}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})).
Remark 5.2.

Note that P​RγPR_{\gamma} does not descend to a homomorphism from Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) to Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})). In fact, an inner automorphism of P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) which reverses the orientation of γ{\gamma} (e.g. a hyperelliptic involution fixing γ{\gamma}) induces on P​Γˇ​(S∖γ){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}) by the above procedure an automorphism which is not inner (it is in the image of Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})) in Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}))).

By Theorem 4.1, there is a natural homomorphism Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})). Composing with P​RγPR_{\gamma}, we get the homomorphism:

P​R¯γ:Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ)).\overline{PR}_{\gamma}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})).

It is easy to see that Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) is contained in the kernel of this homomorphism. So, again by Theorem 4.1, we get a natural homomorphism:

(7) Rγ:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ)).R_{\gamma}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})).

Let δ\delta be a simple closed curve on SS bounding a 22-punctured closed disc DδD_{\delta}. There is then a short exact sequence (cf. (ii) of Theorem 2.3):

(8) 1→τδℤ^→P​Γˇ​(S)δ→P​Γˇ​(S∖Dδ)→1.1\to\tau_{\delta}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\delta}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus D_{\delta})\to 1.

Note that, from [3, Corollary 6.2], it follows that Z⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)δ)=τδℤ^Z({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\delta})=\tau_{\delta}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}.

The same construction used above for a nonseparating curve γ{\gamma} (except that, in this case, since there holds P​Γˇ​(S)δ=P​Γˇ​(S)δ→{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\delta}={\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\delta}}, we do not need to consider orientations) shows that there is a natural homomorphism:

(9) P​R~δ:Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)δ),\tilde{PR}_{\delta}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\delta}),

whose kernel contains Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) and thus descends to a homomorphism:

(10) P​Rδ:Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)δ).PR_{\delta}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\delta}).

Since Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)δ)\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\delta}) preserves the center τδℤ^\tau_{\delta}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} of P​Γˇ​(S)δ{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\delta}, from the short exact sequence (8), we also get a homomorphism:

P​RDδ:Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖Dδ)),PR_{D_{\delta}}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus D_{\delta})),

and then, by Theorem 4.1, a homomorphism:

(11) RDδ:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖Dδ)).R_{D_{\delta}}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus D_{\delta})).

For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1 and γ{\gamma} a simple closed curve on SS which is either nonseparating or bounds a 22-punctured disc, Inn⁡P​Γˇ​(S)γ→\operatorname{Inn}{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}} acts trivially on the procyclic center I^γ=τγℤ^{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}=\tau_{\gamma}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} of P​Γˇ​(S)γ→{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}. Therefore, there is a natural representation, induced by restriction of automorphisms, Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ)→Aut⁡(I^γ)\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma})\to\operatorname{Aut}({\hat{I}}_{\gamma}). Composing with the homomorphism P​R~γ\tilde{PR}_{\gamma} (cf. (6) or (9)), we get a representation X~​(S)γ:Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Aut⁡(I^γ)\tilde{\Chi}(S)_{\gamma}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Aut}({\hat{I}}_{\gamma}).

It is easy to check that the image in Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)) of Inn⁡Γˇ​(S)\operatorname{Inn}{\check{\Gamma}}(S) is contained in the kernel of the representation X~​(S)γ\tilde{\Chi}(S)_{\gamma}. Therefore, again by Theorem 4.1, we get a natural character which only depends on the topological type of γ{\gamma}:

(12) X​(S)γ:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Aut⁡(I^γ)≅ℤ^∗.\Chi(S)_{\gamma}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Aut}({\hat{I}}_{\gamma})\cong{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}^{\ast}.

The following theorem is a key result of this paper:

Theorem 5.3.

Let us assume ∂S=∅{\partial S}=\emptyset and d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1. With the above definitions, we have:

  1. (i)

    For g⁡(S)≥1g(S)\geq 1, let γ{\gamma} be a nonseparating simple closed curve on SS. Then, there is a natural monomorphism:

    Rγ:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))↪Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ)).R_{\gamma}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})).
  2. (ii)

    For n⁡(S)≥2n(S)\geq 2, let δ\delta be a simple closed curve bounding a 22-punctured closed disc DδD_{\delta} on SS. Then, there is a natural monomorphism:

    RDδ:Out𝕀⁡(Γ^​(S))↪Out𝕀⁡(Γ^​(S∖Dδ)).R_{D_{\delta}}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus D_{\delta})).

For the proof of Theorem 5.3, we will need a series of lemmas.

Lemma 5.4.

For g⁡(S)≥1g(S)\geq 1, let γ{\gamma} be a nonseparating simple closed curve on SS. Then, the group Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S)γ)\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma}) identifies with a subgroup of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}) and there is a natural homomorphism:

Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ))×Aut⁡(I^γ)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}))\times\operatorname{Aut}({\hat{I}}_{\gamma})

with kernel Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S)γ)\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma}).

Proof.

The first statement is clear since P​Γˇ​(S)γ→{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}} is a normal subgroup of Γˇ​(S)γ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma}.

By [7, Lemma 7.4], the short exact sequence 1→I^γ→P​Γˇ​(S)γ→→P​Γˇ​(S∖γ)→11\to{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})\to 1 determines an exact sequence:

1→Hom⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ),I^γ)→Aut⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)→Aut⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))×Aut⁡(I^γ).1\to\operatorname{Hom}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}),{\hat{I}}_{\gamma})\to\operatorname{Aut}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})\to\operatorname{Aut}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}))\times\operatorname{Aut}({\hat{I}}_{\gamma}).

By the explicit description of the image of Hom⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ),I^γ)\operatorname{Hom}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}),{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}) in Aut⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)\operatorname{Aut}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}) given in the proof of [7, Lemma 7.4], we see that Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}) has trivial intersection with it. Hence, the natural homomorphism Aut⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)→Aut⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))×Aut⁡(I^γ)\operatorname{Aut}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})\to\operatorname{Aut}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}))\times\operatorname{Aut}({\hat{I}}_{\gamma}) restricts to a monomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)↪Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))×Aut⁡(I^γ)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}))\times\operatorname{Aut}({\hat{I}}_{\gamma}).

Since Z⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)=I^γZ({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})={\hat{I}}_{\gamma}, there is an isomorphism Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)≅Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})\cong\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})) and then a natural monomorphism:

(13) Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)↪Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))×Aut⁡(I^γ).\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}))\times\operatorname{Aut}({\hat{I}}_{\gamma}).

By (i) of Theorem 4.1, there is a natural epimorphisms Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})) with kernel Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ))/Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}))\left/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}))\right..

For n⁡(S)=0n(S)=0, the image of Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S)γ)/Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma})\left/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})\right. in Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})) identifies with such kernel, which implies the lemma in this case.

For n⁡(S)≥1n(S)\geq 1, by (ii) of Theorem 4.1, there is a natural isomorphism:

Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))≅Σn+2×Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ)).\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}))\cong\Sigma_{n+2}\times\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})).

Therefore, an element of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S∖γ))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})) in the image of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}), modulo Inn⁡P​Γˇ​(S∖γ)\operatorname{Inn}{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma}), fixes any Dehn twist about a simple closed curve bounding a disc containing only the two punctures of S∖γS\smallsetminus{\gamma} which are bounded by γ{\gamma}. Lemma 5.5.

For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, g⁡(S)≥0g(S)\geq 0, n⁡(S)≥2n(S)\geq 2 and δ\delta a simple closed curve bounding a 22-punctured closed disc DδD_{\delta} on SS, the group Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S)δ)\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\delta}) identifies with a subgroup of Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)δ)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\delta}) and there is a natural homomorphism:

with kernel Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S)δ)\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\delta}).

Proof.

The proof is essentially the same as that of Lemma 5.4 but simpler. ∎

We will also need the lemma:

Lemma 5.6.

For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, suppose that one of the following hypotheses is satisfied:

We already observed that Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) is contained in the kernel of this homomorphism. Hence, we only need to show the reverse inclusion.

Let f∈ker⁡(Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)γ→)/Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S)γ))f\in\ker(\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\left.\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}})\right/\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\gamma})). Since, for every σ∈Cˇ​(S)d⁡(S)−2{\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S)_{d(S)-2} such that γ∈σ{\gamma}\in{\sigma}, the vertices of the profinite Farey subgraph F^σ⊂CˇP​(S){\widehat{\operatorname{F}}}_{{\sigma}}\subset{\check{C}}_{P}(S) identify with subgroups of the stabilizer P​Γˇ​(S)γ→{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\vec{\gamma}}, the action of ff on the vertices of the procongruence pants complex CˇP​(S){\check{C}}_{P}(S), induced by the natural representation Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Aut⁡(Cˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Aut}({\check{C}}(S)), trivially extends to the identity map on the vertices of all profinite Farey subgraphs F^σ⊂CˇP​(S){\widehat{\operatorname{F}}}_{\sigma}\subset{\check{C}}_{P}(S) such that γ∈σ{\gamma}\in{\sigma}.

Since d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, for γ{\gamma} nonseparating, we have that d⁡(S∖γ)≥1d(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})\geq 1 (resp. d⁡(S∖Dγ)≥1d(S\smallsetminus D_{\gamma})\geq 1 for γ{\gamma} separating). Therefore, the set of profinite Farey subgraphs F^σ⊂CˇP​(S){\widehat{\operatorname{F}}}_{\sigma}\subset{\check{C}}_{P}(S) such that γ∈σ{\gamma}\in{\sigma} is non-empty and, from Lemma 4.2, it follows that f∈Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))f\in\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)). ∎

5.2. Injective functorial homomorphisms

There is a third natural homomorphism between outer 𝕀\mathbb{I}-automorphism groups of procongruence mapping class groups which we need to consider. For SS a closed hyperbolic surface of genus ≥2\geq 2 and P∈SP\in S, let us consider the associated procongruence Birman short exact sequence (cf. [5, Corollary 4.7]):

1→π^1​(S,P)→Γˇ​(S∖P)→Γˇ​(S)→1,1\to{\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(S,P)\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P)\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\to 1,

where a simple generator γ{\gamma} of π1​(S,P)⊂π^1​(S,P)\pi_{1}(S,P)\subset{\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(S,P) is sent by the map π^1​(S,P)→Γˇ​(S∖P){\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(S,P)\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P) to the bounding pair map τγ1​τγ2−1\tau_{{\gamma}_{1}}\tau_{{\gamma}_{2}}^{-1}, where γ1{\gamma}_{1} and γ2{\gamma}_{2} are the boundary components of a tubular neighborhood of γ{\gamma} in SS. In particular, the group π^1​(S,P){\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(S,P) is (topologically) generated in Γˇ​(S∖P){\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P) by such bounding pair maps.

Since, by [7, Theorem 5.5], the action of Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖P))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P)) on the procongruence curve complex Cˇ​(S∖P){\check{C}}(S\smallsetminus P) preserves topological types of simplices, it follows, in particular, that the action of Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖P))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P)) on Γˇ​(S∖P){\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P) preserves the topological type of bounding pair maps associated to annuli on SS containing the puncture and so it preserves the image of π^1​(S,P){\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(S,P) in Γˇ​(S∖P){\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P). An element of Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖P))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P)) then induces an automorphism on the quotient Γˇ​(S∖P)/π^1​(S,P)≅Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P)/{\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(S,P)\cong{\check{\Gamma}}(S).

Therefore, there is a natural homomorphism B~P:Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖P))→Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))\tilde{B}_{P}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P))\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) and then a natural homomorphism:

(14) BP:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖P))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S)).B_{P}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)).

In conclusion, we have constructed three types of natural homomorphisms between outer 𝕀\mathbb{I}-automorphism groups of procongruence mapping class groups:

  1. (i)

    For g⁡(S)≥1g(S)\geq 1, a homomorphism Rγ:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ))R_{\gamma}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})).

  2. (ii)

    For n⁡(S)≥2n(S)\geq 2, a homomorphism RDδ:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖Dδ))R_{D_{\delta}}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus D_{\delta})).

  3. (iii)

    For SS a closed surface, a homomorphism BP:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖P))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))B_{P}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)).

Let SS and S′S^{\prime} be surfaces such that g⁡(S)≥g⁡(S′)g(S)\geq g(S^{\prime}) and χ⁡(S)≤χ⁡(S′)<0\chi(S)\leq\chi(S^{\prime})<0. Cutting SS along g⁡(S)−g⁡(S′)g(S)-g(S^{\prime}) nonseparating simple closed curves and then filling in χ⁡(S′)−χ⁡(S)\chi(S^{\prime})-\chi(S) punctures, we obtain a surface homeomorphic to S′S^{\prime}. Composing g⁡(S)−g⁡(S′)g(S)-g(S^{\prime}) maps of type (i) with χ⁡(S′)−χ⁡(S)\chi(S^{\prime})-\chi(S) maps of type (ii), if n⁡(S′)>0n(S^{\prime})>0, or χ⁡(S′)−χ⁡(S)−1\chi(S^{\prime})-\chi(S)-1 maps of type (ii) and a map of type (iii), if n⁡(S′)=0n(S^{\prime})=0, we obtain a homomorphism:

μS,S′:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S′)).\mu_{S,S^{\prime}}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S^{\prime})).

It is not difficult to check that changing the order of the compositions between the maps of the various types gives the same homomorphism and hence also that the collection of natural homomorphisms {μS,S′}\{\mu_{S,S^{\prime}}\} thus obtained is functorial in the sense that, given surfaces S,S′S,S^{\prime} and S′′S^{\prime\prime} such that g⁡(S)≥g⁡(S′)≥g⁡(S′′)g(S)\geq g(S^{\prime})\geq g(S^{\prime\prime}) and χ⁡(S)≤χ⁡(S′)≤χ⁡(S′′)<0\chi(S)\leq\chi(S^{\prime})\leq\chi(S^{\prime\prime})<0, there holds μS,S′′=μS′,S′′∘μS,S′\mu_{S,S^{\prime\prime}}=\mu_{S^{\prime},S^{\prime\prime}}\circ\mu_{S,S^{\prime}}. By Theorem 5.3, Corollary 3.15 and the above discussion, we have:

Theorem 5.7.

Let SS and S′S^{\prime} be surfaces with empty boundary such that g⁡(S)≥g⁡(S′)g(S)\geq g(S^{\prime}), χ⁡(S)≤χ⁡(S′)\chi(S)\leq\chi(S^{\prime}) and d⁡(S′)≥1d(S^{\prime})\geq 1. Then, there is a natural and functorial monomorphism:

(15) μS,S′:Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))↪Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S′)).\mu_{S,S^{\prime}}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S^{\prime})).
Proof.

We only have to show that the homomorphism BP:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖P))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))B_{P}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) is injective. This follows from the fact that, for γ{\gamma} a nonseparating simple closed curve on S∖PS\smallsetminus P, the composition of BPB_{P} with the map Rγ:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ))R_{\gamma}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})) equals the composition of the map Rγ:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖P))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​((S∖P)∖γ))R_{\gamma}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus P))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}((S\smallsetminus P)\smallsetminus{\gamma})) with the map RDδ:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​((S∖P)∖γ))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S∖γ))R_{D_{\delta}}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}((S\smallsetminus P)\smallsetminus{\gamma}))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\gamma})), where δ\delta is a simple closed curve on (S∖P)∖γ(S\smallsetminus P)\smallsetminus{\gamma} bounding a disc containing two punctures, and we already know (cf. Theorem 5.3) that the latter two homomorphisms are injective. ∎

6. Automorphisms of procongruence mapping class groups

In this section, we will prove the procongruence analogue of Ivanov theorem on automorphism groups of mapping class groups (cf. Theorem A). We will actually prove a more precise and general formulation of this result.

Let us recall that, by definition, the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group comes with a natural character χλ:GT^→ℤ^∗\chi_{\lambda}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}^{\ast} defined by the assignment (f,λ)↦λ(f,{\lambda})\mapsto{\lambda} and such that its composition with the embedding Gℚ⊆GT^G_{\mathbb{Q}}\subseteq\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} is the cyclotomic character. We have:

Theorem 6.1.

Let S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} be a hyperbolic surface with d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1:

  1. (i)

    There is a natural isomorphism:

    Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))≅GT^.\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}.
  2. (ii)

    For (g,n+k)≠(1,2)(g,n+k)\neq(1,2), there is a natural isomorphism:

    Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))≅Σn+k×GT^.\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\Sigma_{n+k}\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}.
  3. (iii)

    There is a natural isomorphism:

    Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))≅GT^.\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\cong\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}.
  4. (iv)

    The outer action of GT^\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} on Γˇ​(S,∂S){\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) of item (iii) restricts to a genuine action on the normal inertia group ∏i=1kτδiℤ^\prod_{i=1}^{k}\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} with the property that each procyclic subgroup τδiℤ^\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} is preserved and acted upon through the character χλ:GT^→ℤ^∗\chi_{\lambda}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}^{\ast}.

  5. (v)

    For S≠S1,2S\neq S_{1,2}, there is a natural isomorphism:

    Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))≅Σn×Σk×GT^.\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\cong\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}.
Remark 6.2.

In the above as in all following statements, ”natural” means that the isomorphisms are compatible with the homomorphisms μS,S′\mu_{S,S^{\prime}} introduced in Section 5.2.

6.1. The proof of Theorem 6.1

By (ii) of Theorem 4.1 (cf. also Theorem 3.12 and Corollary 3.15) and (ii) of Theorem 4.13, we have that (i)⇒\Rightarrow(ii) and (iii)⇒\Rightarrow(v). Therefore, it is enough to prove items (i), (iii) and (iv) of Theorem 6.1. For the proof, we will need the following fundamental lemma, whose proof will be postponed (cf. Section 6.4):

Lemma 6.3.

For a hyperbolic surface SS, there is a natural representation:

Ψ(S,∂S):GT^→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S)).\Psi_{(S,{\partial S})}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})).

In the next two subsections, we will show how Theorem 6.1 follows from Lemma 6.3.

6.2. Lemma 6.3 implies (i) of Theorem 6.1

Let us assume first that SS has empty boundary. By Theorem 5.7, for d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, there is then a natural monomorphism:

μS,S0,5:Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))↪Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S0,5))=GT^.\mu_{S,S_{0,5}}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S_{0,5}))=\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}.

By Lemma 6.3 and Corollary 3.15, there is a homomorphism Ψ(S,∅):GT^→Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))\Psi_{(S,\emptyset)}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) so that we get a series of natural homomorphisms:

GT^→Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))↪GT^,\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\hookrightarrow\widehat{\operatorname{GT}},

which proves that μS,S0,5\mu_{S,S_{0,5}} is surjective and then (i) of Theorem 6.1, for S=S̊S=\ring{S}, follows.

Let now S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k}, with k≥1k\geq 1. By Proposition 3.9 and Corollary 3.15, we already know that Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S12))≅Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S1,11))≅GT^\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S_{1}^{2}))\cong\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S_{1,1}^{1}))\cong\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}, so that we can assume (g,n+k)≠(1,2)(g,n+k)\neq(1,2). Let us also observe that, since P​Γˇ​(S)≅P​Γˇ​(S̊){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)\cong{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S}), by the case S=S̊S=\ring{S}, just proved, of (i) of Theorem 6.1 and (ii) of Theorem 4.1, we have that Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))≅Σn+k×GT^\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\Sigma_{n+k}\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}. Let us then consider the short exact sequence:

1→P​Γˇ​(S)→Γˇ​(S)→Σn×Σk→1.1\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\to\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k}\to 1.

By the above assumptions and [7, Theorem 4.14], we have Z⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))=Z⁡(Γˇ​(S))={1}Z({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))=Z({\check{\Gamma}}(S))=\{1\} and, for n,k≠2n,k\neq 2, there also holds Z⁡(Σn×Σk)={1}Z(\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k})=\{1\}. Therefore, from [24, Lemma 4.2] and Lemma 4.5, it follows that there is a natural isomorphism:

where Inn⁡Γˇ​(S)/Inn⁡P​Γˇ​(S)\operatorname{Inn}{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\left/\operatorname{Inn}{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)\right. is identified, via the isomorphism Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))≅Σn+k×GT^\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\Sigma_{n+k}\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}, with the subgroup Σn×Σk\Sigma_{n}\times\Sigma_{k} of Σn+k\Sigma_{n+k}. For n=2n=2 and k≠2k\neq 2, Lemma 4.5 and an argument similar to the proof of [24, Lemma 4.2] imply that there is a short exact sequence:
