The only choice involved in the definition of F¯\bar{F} is that of the lift f˘∈Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γ^​(Sσ,∂Sσ))\breve{f}\in\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S_{\sigma},{\partial S}_{\sigma})) of the given f∈GT^f\in\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}, which we had identified with an element of Out𝕀⁡(P​Γ^​(Sσ,∂Sσ))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S_{\sigma},{\partial S}_{\sigma})). Therefore, if we let FF be the image of F¯\bar{F} in Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})), the assignment f↦Ff\mapsto F is well defined.

Moreover, following through the definition of F¯\bar{F}, we see that, if f˘1\breve{f}_{1} and f˘2\breve{f}_{2} are lifts of elements f1,f2∈GT^f_{1},f_{2}\in\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}, their product f˘1⋅f˘2\breve{f}_{1}\cdot\breve{f}_{2} is a lift of f1⋅f2∈GT^f_{1}\cdot f_{2}\in\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} with the property that the associated element in Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) is the product F¯1⋅F¯2\bar{F}_{1}\cdot\bar{F}_{2}.

Thus, the assignment f↦Ff\mapsto F determines a homomorphism GT^→Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S))\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})), as claimed in Theorem 6.7. That this representation is faithful, follows by considering its restriction to the subgroup P​Γ^​(S,∂S)σ→{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}}. The last part of the statement of Theorem 6.7 about the action on the central inertia group follows from the construction above.

6.14. Proof of Theorem 6.7 for S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k} and n+k≠0n+k\neq 0

This case of Theorem 6.7 follows from the one considered in the previous section. In fact, the kernel of the natural epimorphism P​Γ^​(Sgk+n,∂Sgk+n)→P​Γ^​(Sg,nk,∂Sg,nk){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S_{g}^{k+n},\partial S_{g}^{k+n})\to{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S_{g,n}^{k},\partial S_{g,n}^{k}) is preserved by the outer action of GT^\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} on P​Γ^​(Sgk+n,∂Sgk+n){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S_{g}^{k+n},\partial S_{g}^{k+n}) as defined in the previous Section 6.13. Therefore, we get a representation ρ^GT^:GT^→Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S))\hat{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,\partial S)), for S=Sg,nkS=S_{g,n}^{k}, with the properties claimed in Theorem 6.7.

6.15. Proof of Theorem 6.7 for S=SgS=S_{g}

The closed surface case of Theorem 6.7 is instead a consequence of the following considerations, which will be fundamental also for the proof of the case g⁡(S)≥3g(S)\geq 3 of Lemma 6.3 given in Section 6.16.

With the notations of Section 6.13, the automorphism F¯\bar{F} restricts on the subgroup P​Γ^​(S,∂S)σ→{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}} of P​Γ^​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) to the automorphism f~∈Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S)σ→)\tilde{f}\in\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}}). We then have:

Lemma 6.19.

Let γ,γ′{\gamma},{\gamma}^{\prime} be simple nonseparating curves on S∖σS\smallsetminus{\sigma} which, together with the boundary curve δ1{\delta}_{1}, bound a 33-holed genus 00 subsurface of SS. Then, the automorphism f~\tilde{f} preserves the conjugacy class in P​Γ^​(S,∂S)σ→{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}} of the procyclic subgroup generated by τγ−1​τγ′\tau_{\gamma}^{-1}\tau_{{\gamma}^{\prime}}.

Proof.

Let us observe again that, by the subgroup congruence property in genus ≤2\leq 2, we have P​Γ^​(S∖σ)=P​Γˇ​(S∖σ){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\sigma})={\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\sigma}) and P​Γ^​(S,∂S)σ→=P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)σ→{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}}={\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}}.

The group Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S)σ→)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}}) acts on the complex of profinite curves Cˇ​(S∖σ){\check{C}}(S\smallsetminus{\sigma}) through the natural homomorphism Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S)σ→)→Aut𝕀⁡(P​Γ^​(S∖σ))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}})\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S\smallsetminus{\sigma})). From [7, Theorem 5.5 and Proposition 7.2], it then follows that the topological type of the bounding pair {γ,γ′}∈Cˇ​(S∖σ)\{{\gamma},{\gamma}^{\prime}\}\in{\check{C}}(S\smallsetminus{\sigma}) is preserved by the action of f~\tilde{f}, which means that f~\tilde{f} maps the pair {γ,γ′,}\{{\gamma},{\gamma}^{\prime},\} to some other bounding pair {f~​(γ),f~​(γ′)}\{\tilde{f}({\gamma}),\tilde{f}({\gamma}^{\prime})\} of the same topological type, that is to say, in the Inn⁡(Γ^​(S,∂S)σ→)\operatorname{Inn}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}})-orbit of {γ,γ′,}\{{\gamma},{\gamma}^{\prime},\}.

Since f~\tilde{f} preserves the procyclic subgroup generated by τδ1\tau_{{\delta}_{1}}, from Theorem 2.7 and Theorem 2.8, it follows that it also preserves the marked topological type of the bounding pair {γ,γ′}\{{\gamma},{\gamma}^{\prime}\}, that is to say, the bounding pair {f~​(γ),f~​(γ′)}\{\tilde{f}({\gamma}),\tilde{f}({\gamma}^{\prime})\} is in the Inn⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S)σ→)\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}})-orbit of {γ,γ′}\{{\gamma},{\gamma}^{\prime}\}. By the construction of the automorphism f~\tilde{f}, we also know that it acts on a nonseparating profinite Dehn twist in P​Γ^​(S,∂S)σ→{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}} by conjugation twisted by the character χλ:GT^→ℤ^∗\chi_{\lambda}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}^{\ast}. These facts then imply that f~\tilde{f} preserves the conjugacy class in P​Γ^​(S,∂S)σ→{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})_{\vec{\sigma}} of the procyclic subgroup generated by τγ−1​τγ′\tau_{\gamma}^{-1}\tau_{{\gamma}^{\prime}}. ∎

Let S¯\overline{S} be the surface obtained glueing a disc DD to the boundary component δ1{\delta}_{1} of SS and let us fix a base point P∈DP\in D. There is then a profinite Birman exact sequence:

(27) 1→π^1​(S¯,P)×τδ1ℤ^→P​Γ^​(S,∂S)→P​Γ^​(S¯,∂S¯)→1,1\to{\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(\overline{S},P)\times\tau_{{\delta}_{1}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}\to{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(\overline{S},\partial\overline{S})\to 1,

where the conjugacy class of τγ−1​τγ′\tau_{\gamma}^{-1}\tau_{{\gamma}^{\prime}} in P​Γ^​(S¯,∂S¯){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(\overline{S},\partial\overline{S}) (topologically) generates the normal subgroup π^1​(S¯,P){\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(\overline{S},P). By Lemma 6.19, the automorphism F¯\bar{F} preserves the conjugacy class in P​Γ^​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) of the procyclic subgroup generated by τγ−1​τγ′\tau_{\gamma}^{-1}\tau_{{\gamma}^{\prime}}. Therefore, the representation ρ^GT^:GT^↪Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S))\hat{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) preserves the normal subgroup π^1​(S¯,P)×τδ1ℤ^{\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(\overline{S},P)\times\tau_{{\delta}_{1}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} of P​Γ^​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) and so induces a representation on the quotient:

ρ^GT^:GT^→Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S¯,∂S¯)).\hat{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(\overline{S},\partial\overline{S})).

That this representation is also faithful follows from its compatibility with the restriction of ρ^GT^\hat{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}} to modular subgroups of P​Γ^​(S¯,∂S¯){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(\overline{S},\partial\overline{S}). Note that, for k=1k=1, the surface S¯\overline{S} is closed and ∂S¯=∅\partial\overline{S}=\emptyset, so that, in particular, we get the closed surface case of Theorem 6.7.

6.16. Proof of Lemma 6.3 for g⁡(S)≥3g(S)\geq 3

The image of the natural representation:

ρ^S:P​Γ^​(S,∂S)→Aut⁡(π^1​(S¯,P)),\hat{\rho}_{S}\colon\thinspace{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(\overline{S},P)),

induced by restriction of inner automorphisms to the normal subgroup OPENπ^1​(S¯,P)){\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(\overline{S},P)) appearing in the profinite Birman exact sequence (27), is precisely the procongruence mapping class group P​Γˇ​(S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S) (cf. [5, Corollary 4.7]).

Let us then show that ρ^GT^:GT^↪Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S))\hat{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) induces a representation:

(28) ρˇGT^:GT^→Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)).\check{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)).

This follows from the lemma:

Lemma 6.20.

The outer automorphisms of P​Γ^​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) in the image of ρ^GT^\hat{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}} preserve the normal subgroup ker⁡ρ^S\ker\hat{\rho}_{S} of P​Γ^​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}).

Proof.

Let ϕ~∈Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S))\tilde{\phi}\in\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) be a lift of an element ϕ∈Im⁡ρ^GT^⊂Out𝕀0⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S))\phi\in\operatorname{Im}\hat{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}}\subset\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})). By Lemma 6.19, we have that ϕ~​(π^1​(S¯,P))=π^1​(S¯,P)\tilde{\phi}({\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(\overline{S},P))={\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(\overline{S},P). Let x∈ker⁡ρ^Sx\in\ker\hat{\rho}_{S}, that is to say an element x∈P​Γ^​(S,∂S)x\in{\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) such that the restriction of inn⁡x\operatorname{inn}x to π^1​(S¯,P){\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(\overline{S},P) is trivial. Then, also ϕ~∘inn⁡x∘ϕ~−1\tilde{\phi}\circ\operatorname{inn}x\circ\tilde{\phi}^{-1} restricts to the trivial automorphism on π^1​(S¯,P){\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(\overline{S},P) and, from the identity ϕ~∘inn⁡x∘ϕ~−1=inn⁡(ϕ~​(x))\tilde{\phi}\circ\operatorname{inn}x\circ\tilde{\phi}^{-1}=\operatorname{inn}(\tilde{\phi}(x)), it follows that ϕ~​(x)∈ker⁡ρ^S\tilde{\phi}(x)\in\ker\hat{\rho}_{S}. ∎

Note that the representation ρˇGT^\check{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}} (28) is defined for every hyperbolic nonclosed surface. Composing with the natural homomorphism Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S̊))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S})) (cf. Theorem 3.12 and Theorem 4.1), we then get the natural representation:

Ψ(S̊,∅):GT^→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S̊)).\Psi_{(\ring{S},\emptyset)}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S})).

If S̊=S′∖P\ring{S}=S^{\prime}\smallsetminus P, where S′S^{\prime} is a closed surface, we can further compose Ψ(S̊,∅)\Psi_{(\ring{S},\emptyset)} with the homomorphism (14) BP:Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S̊))→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S′))B_{P}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(\ring{S}))\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S^{\prime})), thus obtaining the representation:

Ψ(S′,∅):GT^→Out𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S′)).\Psi_{(S^{\prime},\emptyset)}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\to\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S^{\prime})).

By construction, these representations are functorial with respect to the restriction to subsurfaces of SS. This proves Lemma 6.3 for all the cases when g⁡(S)≥3g(S)\geq 3 and ∂S=∅{\partial S}=\emptyset.

The representation Ψ(S,∂S)\Psi_{(S,{\partial S})}, for g⁡(S)≥3g(S)\geq 3 and ∂S≠∅{\partial S}\neq\emptyset, is then obtained composing Ψ(S~,∅)\Psi_{({\widetilde{S}},\emptyset)}, for S~=Sg,n+2​k{\widetilde{S}}=S_{g,n+2k} as in Remark 2.4, with the homomorphism R(S,∂S)R_{(S,{\partial S})} (22).

6.17. The automorphism group of the procongruence Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower

In the landmark paper [9], Drinfeld, following Grothendieck’s [12, Esquisse d’un Programme], speculated that the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group, which is defined taking into account only the first two levels of the genus 00 stage of the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower, naturally acts on the full tower and that, moreover, this action induces an isomorphism:

Conjecture 6.21 (Drinfeld-Grothendieck).

GT^≅Aut⁡(𝔗^out)\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\cong\operatorname{Aut}(\hat{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}).

Combining Conjecture 6.21 with Conjecture 2.10 yields the Grothendieck-Teichmüller conjecture:

Conjecture 6.22.

GT^≅Gℚ\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\cong G_{\mathbb{Q}}.

As an application of Theorem 6.1, we will now prove the following procongruence version of Conjecture 6.21:

Theorem 6.23.

There is a natural isomorphism GT^≅Aut⁡(𝔗ˇout)\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\cong\operatorname{Aut}(\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}).

Of course, assuming the congruence subgroup property, the profinite and procongruence versions of the Drinfeld-Grothendieck conjecture are just equivalent. Even if this is still an open problem, the following immediate consequence of Theorem 6.7 shows that there are no additional restrictions coming from the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower:

Corollary 6.24.

There is a natural faithful representation ρ^GT^:GT^↪Aut⁡(𝔗^out)\hat{\rho}_{\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}}\colon\thinspace\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(\hat{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}). In particular, Conjecture 2.10 implies Conjecture 6.22.

6.18. Proof of Theorem 6.23

Let us observe that there are natural homomorphisms:

tr^S:Aut⁡(𝔗^out)→Out⁡(P​Γ^​(S,∂S))andtrˇS:Aut⁡(𝔗ˇout)→Out⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)),\hat{\operatorname{tr}}_{S}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Aut}(\hat{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}})\to\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\widehat{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\hskip 14.22636pt\mbox{and}\hskip 14.22636pt\check{\operatorname{tr}}_{S}\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Aut}(\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}})\to\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})),

defined restricting an automorphism of the full tower to one of its components.

Lemma 6.25.

There holds Im⁡tr^S⊆Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Im}\hat{\operatorname{tr}}_{S}\subseteq\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) and Im⁡trˇS⊆Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Im}\check{\operatorname{tr}}_{S}\subseteq\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})).

Proof.

The proof is exactly the same for the profinite and the procongruence case. Let us then prove the lemma for the procongruence Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower which is the case we need for the proof of Theorem 6.23.

Let us show first that, for ∂S=∪i=1kδi≠∅{\partial S}=\cup_{i=1}^{k}{\delta}_{i}\neq\emptyset, the image of Aut⁡(𝔗ˇout)\operatorname{Aut}(\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}) in the group Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) preserve each procyclic subgroup τδiℤ^\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}, for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k. Let S~i\tilde{S}_{i} be the surface obtained attaching a 11-punctured disc to the boundary component δi{\delta}_{i} of SS. The map S→S~iS\to\tilde{S}_{i} then induces, in the procongruence Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower, the homomorphism of procongruence pure relative mapping class groups P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)→P​Γˇ​(S~i,∂S~i){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(\tilde{S}_{i},\partial\tilde{S}_{i}). By definition, an element of Aut⁡(𝔗ˇout)\operatorname{Aut}(\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}) is compatible with this homomorphism and so preserves its kernel which is precisely the procyclic subgroup τδiℤ^\tau_{{\delta}_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}, for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k.

In order to show that the image of Aut⁡(𝔗ˇout)\operatorname{Aut}(\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}) in Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) preserves the conjugacy class of the procyclic subgroup generated by the Dehn twist τγ\tau_{\gamma}, where γ{\gamma} is any nonperipheral simple closed curve on SS, it is enough to observe that there is an embedding S′↪SS^{\prime}\hookrightarrow S in 𝒮{\mathcal{S}} such that γ{\gamma} is in the image of a boundary component of S′S^{\prime}. From the previous case, it then follows that an automorphism of Aut⁡(𝔗ˇout)\operatorname{Aut}(\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}) is compatible with the associated homomorphism P​Γˇ​(S′,∂S′)→P​Γˇ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S^{\prime},{\partial S}^{\prime})\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) only if its image in Out⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Out}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})) preserves the conjugacy class of τγℤ^\tau_{\gamma}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}}. ∎

Remark 6.26.

Lemma 6.25 shows, in particular, that the inertia condition of Grothendieck-Teichmüller theory is intrinsic to the whole Grothendieck-Teichmüller tower, even though it may not be intrinsic to the single components (the conjecture, however, is that, for d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1 and P​Γˇ​(S,∂S){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}) center free, it is).

From Theorem 6.1, it follows that there is a natural monomorphism GT^↪Aut⁡(𝔗ˇout)\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}}). In order to prove that Aut⁡(𝔗ˇout)≅GT^\operatorname{Aut}(\check{\mathfrak{T}}^{\mathrm{out}})\cong\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}, it is then enough to determine the image of trˇS\check{\operatorname{tr}}_{S}, for S=SgkS=S_{g}^{k} and d⁡(S)>2d(S)>2.

By (v) of Theorem 6.1, for S=SgkS=S_{g}^{k} and d⁡(S)>2d(S)>2, we have Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))≅Σk×GT^\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))\cong\Sigma_{k}\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}} so that, by Lemma 6.25, to prove Theorem 6.23, it is enough to show that Im⁡trˇS\operatorname{Im}\check{\operatorname{tr}}_{S} has trivial projection to Σk\Sigma_{k}, for S≠S1,2S\neq S_{1,2}. This claim follows considering the natural maps S→S¯iS\to\overline{S}_{i}, where S¯i\overline{S}_{i} is the surface obtained glueing a disc DD to the boundary component δi{\delta}_{i} of S=SgkS=S_{g}^{k}, for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k. In fact, an element of Out𝕀⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})), which projects to a nontrivial element of the symmetric group Σk≅Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S,∂S))/Inn⁡(P​Γˇ​(S,∂S))\Sigma_{k}\cong\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S}))/\operatorname{Inn}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})), does not preserve the kernel π^1​(S¯i,P)×τδiℤ^{\widehat{\pi}}_{1}(\overline{S}_{i},P)\times\tau_{\delta_{i}}^{\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}} of the homomorphism P​Γˇ​(S,∂S)→P​Γˇ​(S¯i,∂S¯i){\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S,{\partial S})\to{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(\overline{S}_{i},\partial\overline{S}_{i}), for i=1,…,ki=1,\ldots,k (cf. (27)).

7. The automorphism group of the arithmetic procongruence mapping class group

In this section, we assume that SS is a hyperbolic surface without boundary.

7.1. The arithmetic profinite mapping class group

By Grothendieck theory of the étale fundamental group, for a geometric base point ξ¯\overline{\xi} of the moduli stack ℳ​(S)ℚ{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}, the structural morphism ℳ​(S)ℚ→Spec⁡(ℚ){\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}\to\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{Q}) induces the short exact sequence of étale fundamental groups:

(29) 1→π1et​(ℳ​(S)ℚ¯,ξ¯)→π1et​(ℳ​(S)ℚ,ξ¯)→Gℚ→1.1\to\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}},\overline{\xi})\to\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}},\overline{\xi})\to G_{\mathbb{Q}}\to 1.

The left hand term π1et​(ℳ​(S)ℚ¯,ξ¯)\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}},\overline{\xi}) of this short exact sequence is the geometric étale fundamental group of ℳ​(S)ℚ{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}. It is naturally isomorphic to the profinite completion of the topological fundamental group, with base point the image of ξ¯ℂ\overline{\xi}_{\mathbb{C}}, of the complex analytic stack associated to the complex DM stack ℳ​(S)ℂ{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{C}}.

Thus, π1et​(ℳ​(S)ℚ¯,ξ¯)\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}},\overline{\xi}) can be identified with the profinite completion Γ^​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) of the mapping class group Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) associated to the surface SS. To be more precise, this identification is determined by the isotopy class of a diffeomorphism S→(𝒞​(S)ξ¯×ℂ)anS\to({\mathscr{C}}(S)_{\overline{\xi}}\times\mathbb{C})^{\mathrm{an}} compatible with the orientations.

A (tangential) rational point on ℳ​(S)ℚ{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}} determines a splitting of the short exact sequence (29). There is then a (faithful) representation ρ^ℚ:Gℚ→Aut⁡(Γ^​(S))\hat{\rho}_{\mathbb{Q}}\colon\thinspace G_{\mathbb{Q}}\to\operatorname{Aut}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)) which induces an isomorphism of profinite groups:

π1et​(ℳ​(S)ℚ,ξ¯)≅Γ^​(S)⋊ρ^ℚGℚ.\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}},\overline{\xi})\cong{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)\rtimes_{\hat{\rho}_{\mathbb{Q}}}G_{\mathbb{Q}}.

It is natural to denote by Γ^​(S)ℚ{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}} the profinite group π1et​(ℳ​(S)ℚ,ξ¯)\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}},\overline{\xi}) which we will call the arithmetic profinite mapping class group. Let P​Γ^​(S)\mathrm{P}{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) be the profinite completion of the pure mapping class group P​Γ​(S)\mathrm{P}{\Gamma}(S) associated to the surface SS. After the identification of π1et​(P​ℳ​(S)ℚ¯,ξ¯)\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}},\overline{\xi}) with P​Γ^​(S)\mathrm{P}{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S), we will also put P​Γ^​(S)ℚ:=π1et​(P​ℳ​(S)ℚ,ξ¯)\mathrm{P}{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}:=\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}},\overline{\xi}).

7.2. The arithmetic procongruence mapping class group

Let 𝒞⁡(S)→ℳ⁡(S){\mathscr{C}}(S)\to{\mathcal{M}}(S) be the universal punctured curve over the moduli stack ℳ⁡(S){\mathcal{M}}(S) and P​𝒞​(S)→P​ℳ​(S)\mathrm{P}{\mathscr{C}}(S)\to\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S) be the universal curve over the moduli stack P​ℳ​(S)\mathrm{P}{\mathcal{M}}(S).

Let 𝒞​(S)ξ¯{\mathscr{C}}(S)_{\overline{\xi}} be the fiber over the geometric point ξ¯∈ℳ​(S)ℚ\overline{\xi}\in{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}} of the universal curve 𝒞⁡(S)→ℳ⁡(S){\mathscr{C}}(S)\to{\mathcal{M}}(S) and ξ~∈𝒞​(S)ξ¯\tilde{\xi}\in{\mathscr{C}}(S)_{\overline{\xi}} a geometric point. There is then a short exact sequence of algebraic fundamental groups:

1→π1et​(𝒞​(S)ξ¯,ξ~)→π1et​(𝒞​(S)ℚ,ξ~)→π1et​(ℳ​(S)ℚ,ξ¯)→1.1\to\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathscr{C}}(S)_{\overline{\xi}},\tilde{\xi})\to\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathscr{C}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}},\tilde{\xi})\to\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}},\overline{\xi})\to 1.

The associated outer representation

ρSet:π1et​(ℳ​(S)ℚ,ξ¯)→Out⁡(π1et​(𝒞​(S)ξ¯,ξ~)){\rho}^{\mathrm{et}}_{S}\colon\thinspace\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}},\overline{\xi})\to\operatorname{Out}(\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathscr{C}}(S)_{\overline{\xi}},\tilde{\xi}))

is called the universal étale monodromy representation.

After identifying π1et​(ℳ​(S)ℚ¯,ξ¯)\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}},\overline{\xi}) with Γ^​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S) and π1et​(ℳ​(S)ℚ,ξ¯)\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{et}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}},\overline{\xi}) with Γ^​(S)ℚ{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}, we then let

Γˇ​(S):=ρSet​(Γ^​(S)) and Γˇ​(S)ℚ:=ρSet​(Γ^​(S)ℚ){\check{\Gamma}}(S):={\rho}^{\mathrm{et}}_{S}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\hskip 28.45274pt\mbox{ and }\hskip 28.45274pt{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}:={\rho}^{\mathrm{et}}_{S}({\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})

and call them, respectively, the procongruence and the arithmetic procongruence mapping class groups. The pure procongruence and arithmetic procongruence mapping class groups are then defined by:

P​Γˇ​(S):=ρSet​(P​Γ^​(S)) and P​Γˇ​(S)ℚ:=ρSet​(P​Γ^​(S)ℚ).{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S):={\rho}^{\mathrm{et}}_{S}(\mathrm{P}{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S))\hskip 28.45274pt\mbox{ and }\hskip 28.45274pt{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}:={\rho}^{\mathrm{et}}_{S}(\mathrm{P}{\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}).

Hoshi and Mochizuki in [15] (see also [3, Corollary 7.10]) showed that the kernel of ρSet{\rho}^{\mathrm{et}}_{S} identifies with the congruence kernel, i.e. the kernel of the natural epimorphism Γ^​(S)→Γˇ​(S){\widehat{\Gamma}}(S)\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S). Therefore, the short exact sequence (29) gives rise to a short exact sequence:

(30) 1→Γˇ​(S)→Γˇ​(S)ℚ→Gℚ→1,1\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\to{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}\to G_{\mathbb{Q}}\to 1,

such that the associated outer representation ρℚ:Gℚ→Out⁡(Γˇ​(S))\rho_{\mathbb{Q}}\colon\thinspace G_{\mathbb{Q}}\to\operatorname{Out}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) is faithful.

The splitting of the short exact sequence (29) determined by a tangential base point also determines a splitting of the short exact sequence (30). There is then a (faithful) representation ρˇℚ:Gℚ→Aut⁡(Γˇ​(S))\check{\rho}_{\mathbb{Q}}\colon\thinspace G_{\mathbb{Q}}\to\operatorname{Aut}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) which induces an isomorphism of profinite groups:

(31) Γˇ​(S)ℚ≅Γˇ​(S)⋊ρˇℚGℚ.{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}\cong{\check{\Gamma}}(S)\rtimes_{\check{\rho}_{\mathbb{Q}}}G_{\mathbb{Q}}.

7.3. The automorphism group of the arithmetic procongruence mapping class group

Let us define inertia and decomposition groups for the arithmetic procongruence mapping class group Γˇ​(S)ℚ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}:

Definition 7.1.

Let UU be an open subgroup of Γˇ​(S)ℚ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}. For σ={γ0,…,γk}∈Cˇ​(S){\sigma}=\{{\gamma}_{0},\ldots,{\gamma}_{k}\}\in{\check{C}}(S), the inertia group I^σ​(U){\hat{I}}_{\sigma}(U) is the closed abelian subgroup of UU topologically generated by the powers of the profinite Dehn twists parameterized by σ{\sigma} and contained in UU. The decomposition group Dσ​(U)D_{\sigma}(U) is then the normalizer of I^σ​(U){\hat{I}}_{\sigma}(U) in UU.

Remark 7.2.

Since all closed strata of ℳ¯​(S){\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(S) are defined over ℚ\mathbb{Q} and contain ℚ\mathbb{Q}-rational points, for every σ∈Cˇ​(S){\sigma}\in{\check{C}}(S), there is a splitting of the short exact sequence (30) such that the action ρ~ℚ:Gℚ→Aut⁡(Γˇ​(S))\tilde{\rho}_{\mathbb{Q}}\colon\thinspace G_{\mathbb{Q}}\to\operatorname{Aut}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) preserves the stabilizer Γˇ​(S)σ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\sigma} and so the associated isomorphism (31) induces an isomorphism Dσ​(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)≅Γˇ​(S)σ⋊ρ~ℚGℚD_{\sigma}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\cong{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\sigma}\rtimes_{\tilde{\rho}_{\mathbb{Q}}}G_{\mathbb{Q}}.

Definition 7.3.

For UU an open subgroup of Γˇ​(S)ℚ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}, we define:

  1. (i)

    Aut𝔻⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{D}}(U) is the closed subgroup of Aut⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}(U) consisting of those elements which preserve the set of decomposition groups {Dγ​(U)}γ∈ℒ^​(S)0\{D_{\gamma}(U)\}_{{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0}}.

  2. (ii)

    Aut𝕀⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(U) is the closed subgroup of Aut⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}(U) consisting of those elements which preserve the set of inertia groups {I^γ​(U)}γ∈ℒ^​(S)0\{{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}(U)\}_{{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(S)_{0}}.

  3. (iii)

    Aut𝕀0⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}(U) is the closed subgroup of Aut𝕀⁡(U)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}(U) consisting of those elements which preserve the set of inertia groups {I^γ​(U)}γ∈ℒ^ns​(S)\{{\hat{I}}_{\gamma}(U)\}_{{\gamma}\in\widehat{\mathcal{L}}^{\mathrm{ns}}(S)}.

Remark 7.4.

A result similar to (i) of Proposition 3.5 holds for all the groups of automorphisms defined above.

With the above notation, [7, Theorem 9.16] states, in particular, that, for UU an open normal subgroup of Γˇ​(S)ℚ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}} and S≠S1,2,S2S\neq S_{1,2},S_{2}, we have:

(32) Aut𝔻⁡(U)=Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)≅Γˇ​(S)ℚ.\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{D}}(U)=\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\cong{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}.

Thanks to the results of Section 3.3, we then get the following generalization of [18, Corollary C]:

Corollary 7.5.

For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, we have:

Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)ℚ)≅Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)=Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ).\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\cong\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})=\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}).
Proof.

For S≠S1,2S\neq S_{1,2} and S2S_{2}, the centralizer of P​Γˇ​(S)ℚ{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}} in Γˇ​(S)ℚ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}} is trivial. Therefore, since P​Γˇ​(S)ℚ{\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}} is an 𝕀0\mathbb{I}_{0}-characteristic subgroup of Γˇ​(S)ℚ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}, by [7, Lemma 3.3], Theorem 3.12, item (i) of Proposition 3.7 and the identity (32), for S≠S1,2S\neq S_{1,2} and S2S_{2}, there is a series of natural monomorphisms

Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)↪Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)↪Aut𝕀0⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)ℚ)↪Aut𝔻⁡(P​Γˇ​(S)ℚ)=Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{D}}({\mathrm{P}\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})=\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})

and the conclusion follows.

The cases S=S1,2S=S_{1,2} and S2S_{2} can be reduced to the above observing that Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)=Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ/Z⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})=\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}/Z({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})) (cf. the proofs of (ii) of Proposition 3.9 and of Proposition 6.9). ∎

7.4. The extended mapping class group

The extended mapping class group Γ±​(S){\Gamma}^{\pm}(S) is the group of isotopy classes of all diffeomorphisms of SS. If χℝ:Γ±​(S)→{±1}\chi_{\mathbb{R}}\colon\thinspace{\Gamma}^{\pm}(S)\to\{\pm 1\} denotes the orientation character, there is a short exact sequence:

(33) 1→Γ⁡(S)→Γ±​(S)→χℝ{±1}→1.1\to{\Gamma}(S)\to{\Gamma}^{\pm}(S)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\chi_{\mathbb{R}}}}{{\to}}\{\pm 1\}\to 1.

Note that the choice of any antiholomorphic involution on SS splits this sequence.

The moduli stack ℳ​(S)ℝ{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{R}} is a real model of the complex moduli stack ℳ​(S)ℂ{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{C}}. Hence, the latter carries an antiholomorphic involution ι:ℳ​(S)ℂ→ℳ​(S)ℂ\iota\colon\thinspace{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{C}}\to{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{C}} associated to such a real model. There is a notion of equivariant fundamental group associated to (ℳ​(S)ℂ,ι)({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{C}},\iota) (cf. [17, Section 3]) and, for a base point [C]∈ℳ​(S)ℝ[C]\in{\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{R}}, we let

π1ℝ​(ℳ​(S)ℝ,[C]):=π1equiv​((ℳ​(S)ℂ/⟨ι⟩),[C]).\pi_{1}^{\mathbb{R}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{R}},[C]):=\pi_{1}^{\mathrm{equiv}}(({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{C}}/\langle\iota\rangle),[C]).

The equivariant fundamental group π1ℝ​(ℳ​(S)ℝ,[C])\pi_{1}^{\mathbb{R}}({\mathcal{M}}(S)_{\mathbb{R}},[C]) then identifies with the extended mapping class group Γ±​(S){\Gamma}^{\pm}(S) and the short exact sequence (33) identifies with the associated short exact sequence (cf. [17, Proposition 3.2]). Let us also observe that, in this setting, the orientation group {±1}\{\pm 1\} identifies with the absolute Galois group of the reals GℝG_{\mathbb{R}}.

7.5. Automorphisms of extended mapping class group

Let us denote respectively by Aut𝕀0⁡(Γ⁡(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\Gamma}(S)) and Aut𝕀0⁡(Γ±​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\Gamma}^{\pm}(S))) the group of automorphisms of Γ⁡(S){\Gamma}(S) and Γ±​(S){\Gamma}^{\pm}(S) which preserve the conjugacy class of a cyclic subgroup generated by a Dehn twist about a nonseparating simple closed curve.

A classical result by Ivanov and McCarthy (cf. [20, Theorem 2] and [23, Theorem 1]) asserts that, for d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1 and S≠S1,2,S2S\neq S_{1,2},S_{2} (or, equivalently, if Z⁡(Γ⁡(S))={1}Z({\Gamma}(S))=\{1\}), there holds:

Aut⁡(Γ⁡(S))=Aut𝕀0⁡(Γ⁡(S))≅Aut𝕀0⁡(Γ±​(S))=Aut⁡(Γ±​(S))=Inn⁡(Γ±​(S)).\operatorname{Aut}({\Gamma}(S))=\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\Gamma}(S))\cong\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\Gamma}^{\pm}(S))=\operatorname{Aut}({\Gamma}^{\pm}(S))=\operatorname{Inn}({\Gamma}^{\pm}(S)).

In particular, in this case, there is also a natural isomorphism Out⁡(Γ⁡(S))≅Gℝ\operatorname{Out}({\Gamma}(S))\cong G_{\mathbb{R}}.

7.6. Comparing automorphism groups

As observed in the proof of [7, Theorem 9.16], Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) is a characteristic subgroup of Γˇ​(S)ℚ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}. From [3, Proposition 3.9] and [7, Lemma 3.3], it then follows that, for d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, the natural homomorphism Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)→Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) is injective. A natural question is whether, in analogy with the extended mapping class group case, this is actually an isomorphism:

Question 7.6.

For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, is there a natural isomorphism:

Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)≅Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))​?\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\cong\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))?

Otherwise stated, does every 𝕀0\mathbb{I}_{0}-automorphism of Γˇ​(S){\check{\Gamma}}(S) extend to Γˇ​(S)ℚ{\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}?

By Corollary 7.5, we then have:

Corollary 7.7.

A positive answer to Question 7.6 implies that, for d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, there is a natural isomorphism

Out𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))≅GT^≅Gℚ.\operatorname{Out}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\cong G_{\mathbb{Q}}.
Proof.

The conclusion follows from the series of isomorphisms:

Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))≅Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)≅Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ),\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\cong\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\cong\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}),

dividing out by the normal subgroup Inn⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Inn}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) and applying the first item of Theorem 6.1. ∎

7.7. Automorphisms of the procongruence curve complex

The automorphism group Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}}) acts on the procongruence curve complex Cˇ​(S){\check{C}}(S) through the natural homomorphism Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)→Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))=Aut𝕀⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))=\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) considered in Section 7.6.

Proposition 7.8.

For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, there is a natural faithful representation:

ψ:Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)↪Aut⁡(Cˇ​(S)).\psi\colon\thinspace\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}({\check{C}}(S)).
Proof.

As observed in Section 7.6, the homomorphism Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)→Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\to\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)) is injective. The conclusion then follows from [7, Theorem 7.3, (ii)]. ∎

Ivanov’s fundamental theorem on automorphisms of curve complexes can be formulated, in our terminology, saying that, for d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1 and S≠S1,2,S2S\neq S_{1,2},S_{2}, there is a natural isomorphism (cf. [20, Theorem 1]):

Aut⁡(Γ±​(S))=Aut𝕀0⁡(Γ±​(S))=Aut𝕀⁡(Γ±​(S))≅Aut⁡(C⁡(S)).\operatorname{Aut}({\Gamma}^{\pm}(S))=\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\Gamma}^{\pm}(S))=\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}}({\Gamma}^{\pm}(S))\cong\operatorname{Aut}(C(S)).

A similar question can then be asked for the arithmetic procongruence mapping class group:

Question 7.9.

For d⁡(S)>1d(S)>1, is there a natural isomorphism:

Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)≅Aut⁡(Cˇ​(S))​?\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\cong\operatorname{Aut}({\check{C}}(S))?

By [7, Theorem 7.3, (ii)] and Proposition 7.8, with the above hypotheses, there is a series of monomorphisms:

Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S)ℚ)↪Aut𝕀0⁡(Γˇ​(S))↪Aut⁡(Cˇ​(S)).\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S)_{\mathbb{Q}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}^{\mathbb{I}_{0}}({\check{\Gamma}}(S))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}({\check{C}}(S)).

Therefore, a positive answer to Question 7.9 implies a positive answer to Question 7.6.
